definition_zh: 达到；获得
definition_en: to reach a goal or level after effort, or to gain something
core_image: 手终于够到高处的横杆
scene: 她练了三年才拿到那张证书。After years of study she attained her goal.
sceneCN: 这里 attain 是「达到」（第 1 个义项：经过努力抵达目标）；句意是多年学习后她达到了目标。

senses.title: Reach a goal
senses.definition: to reach a goal, level or age after effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力抵达某个目标、水平或年龄
senses.example: After years of study she attained her goal.
senses.exampleCN: 多年学习之后她达到了目标。
senses.why: Attain comes from Latin attingere, 'to touch', from ad- 'to' and tangere 'to touch', so success is pictured as a hand finally reaching the bar.
senses.whyCN: attain 源自拉丁语 attingere「触到」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成，成功被画成一只手终于够到横杆。

senses.title: Gain or acquire
senses.definition: to gain something such as a reputation or a position
senses.definitionCN: 取得名声、地位等抽象之物
senses.example: He attained a reputation for honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 他获得了诚实的名声。
senses.why: What a hand can touch includes not only a height but also honour and rank, so the reaching verb comes to mean acquiring.
senses.whyCN: 手能够到的不只是高度，还有荣誉与地位，于是这个「够到」的动词就有了「获得」的含义。

intro.en: Attain is a Latin word of touching, and achievement is pictured as reaching something.
intro.cn: attain 是拉丁语中表示「触碰」的词，成就被画成够到某物。

items.en: tangere meant 'to touch'.
items.cn: tangere 意为「触碰」。

items.en: attingere meant 'to touch or reach'.
items.cn: attingere 意为「触到、够到」。

items.en: ateindre meant 'to reach a goal'.
items.cn: ateindre 意为「抵达目标」。

items.en: English attain covered reaching and gaining.
items.cn: 英语 attain 兼指达到与获得。

items.en: The word now sounds formal and is common in writing.
items.cn: 这个词如今偏正式，常见于书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tain stem; the near-meaning group gives verbs of reaching and winning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tain 词干；近义组是表示抵达与取得的动词。

normalIntro.en: To attain is to get your hand on the bar at last.
normalIntro.cn: attain 就是手终于搭上那根横杆。

normal.en: It is formal; in speech people usually say reach or achieve.
normal.cn: 它偏正式，口语里更常说 reach 或 achieve。

normal.en: The object is often abstract: a goal, a level, a standard.
normal.cn: 宾语常是抽象名词：目标、水平、标准。

normal.en: The noun is attainment, not attain.
normal.cn: 名词是 attainment。

normal.en: The tain part also appears in contain and retain.
normal.cn: tain 这一部分也出现在 contain 与 retain 中。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TAIN.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See fingers closing around a high bar.
abstract.cn: 想象手指终于扣住高处横杆。

abstract.en: See a certificate handed over after long practice.
abstract.cn: 想象长期练习后递来的一纸证书。

abstract.en: See a line on a chart finally touched.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的那条线终于被碰到。

examples.en: After years of study she attained her goal.
examples.cn: 多年学习之后她达到了目标。

examples.en: He attained a reputation for honesty.
examples.cn: 他获得了诚实的名声。

examples.en: The team attained the highest standard in the test.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在测试中达到了最高标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tain（触）：手向高处伸去，终于触到，就是达到；够到名声与地位，就是获得。

root: 源自拉丁语 attingere「触到」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成，经古法语 ateindre 进入英语；由「够到」具体高度引申为达到目标与获得名声。

sensesIntro.en: Height and honour are both things a reaching hand can close on.
sensesIntro.cn: 高度与荣誉，都是伸出的手能够握住的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers touching the bar.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖碰到横杆。

intro.en: The tain root, 'to hold or touch', also shapes contain, retain and maintain.
intro.cn: 词根 tain 意为「握住、触及」，也构成 contain、retain 与 maintain。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere, 'to touch', is the source; its participle tactus gives tact and contact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere「触」是来源，其分词 tactus 产生了 tact 与 contact。

definition_zh: adj. 可以达到的；能够获得的（目标、水平、结果）
definition_en: Able to be reached, achieved or obtained, especially of a goal or standard that is realistic.
core_image: 伸手就能碰到的那根横杆
scene: 教练把跳高横杆降到学生平时能过的高度，说这样目标才有意义。The coach lowered the bar to a height that was attainable for every student.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attainable 指目标在能力范围之内，努力之后确实能够达到。

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: A goal within reach
senses.definition: of an aim, level or result that a person can realistically reach with effort
senses.definitionCN: 指目标、水平或结果在努力之后确实能够达到
senses.example: She set an attainable target of ten pages a day.
senses.exampleCN: 她定了每天十页这个可达成的目标。
senses.why: The word joins attain, to reach, with -able, capable of, so it literally means reachable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 attain「达到」加 -able「能够……的」构成，字面就是「可达到的」。

senses.title: Available to be obtained
senses.definition: of a resource, status or benefit that can actually be got or secured
senses.definitionCN: 指资源、地位或利益实际上可以取得或获得
senses.example: Free childcare is attainable only in a few districts.
senses.exampleCN: 免费托育只在少数几个区才能获得。
senses.why: Once reaching a height was clear, the same suffix pattern covered getting hold of anything desired.
senses.whyCN: 「达到某个高度」清楚之后，同一后缀模式也覆盖了「取得任何想要的东西」。

intro.en: Attainable is attain plus -able; attain comes from Old French ataindre, from Latin attingere, to touch upon, from ad-, to, and tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: attainable 是 attain 加 -able；attain 来自古法语 ataindre，出自拉丁语 attingere「触及」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成。

items.en: The root tag- meant to touch, the physical act behind a whole family of contact words.
items.cn: 词根 tag- 意为「触碰」，是一整族接触类词背后的身体动作。

items.en: Latin tangere meant to touch, giving tangent, contact and contingent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tangere 意为「触」，产生 tangent、contact 与 contingent。

items.en: With ad-, to, added, attingere meant to touch upon, to reach as far as a point.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」，attingere 意为「触及」，即延伸到某一点。

items.en: Old French ataindre kept the sense of reaching a place or a person.
items.cn: 古法语 ataindre 保留了「抵达某地或某人」的意思。

items.en: Middle English atteynen meant to reach or arrive at, later spelled attain.
items.cn: 中古英语 atteynen 意为「达到、抵达」，后来拼作 attain。

items.en: English added -able in the sixteenth century to say that a goal could be reached.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪加上 -able，用来表示某个目标能够达到。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the attain family and one familiar -able word; the near-meaning group lists other words for a goal that can be met.
note.cn: 形近组保留 attain 词族和一个常见的 -able 词；近义组列出其他表示目标能够达成的词。

entries.definition: Able to be kept up over time.

normalIntro.en: Attainable splits into attain plus -able: if you can attain it, it is attainable.
normalIntro.cn: attainable 拆成 attain 加 -able：能达到的，就是 attainable。

normal.en: Attain means reach; -able means can be.
normal.cn: attain 意为达到，-able 意为「可以被」。

normal.en: The opposite adds un-: unattainable.
normal.cn: 反义加 un- 就成 unattainable。

normal.en: Goals should be challenging yet attainable.
normal.cn: 目标应当有挑战但仍可达成。

normal.en: The noun is attainability, not attainableness.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 attainability，不用 attainableness。

normal.en: It usually sits before goal, target or standard.
normal.cn: 它通常放在 goal、target 或 standard 之前。

abstract.en: Picture a high-jump bar set at your own height.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高横杆设在你自己能够的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine a shelf just within your fingertips.
abstract.cn: 想象一层刚好在指尖之内的架子。

abstract.en: Think of a plan whose last step is possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一份最后一步确实可行的计划。

examples.en: The salary is attainable after two years.
examples.cn: 两年后这份薪水是可以拿到的。

examples.en: Make the first milestone easily attainable.
examples.cn: 把第一个里程碑定得容易达到。

examples.en: Such purity is not attainable at home.
examples.cn: 这样的纯度在家无法达到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：attain「达到」+ -able「可以……的」——能够达到的，就是 attainable。

root: 拉丁语 tangere「触」加 ad-「向」成 attingere「触及」，经古法语 ataindre 入英语作 attain「达到」；再加 -able 表「可以被达到」，即 attainable。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same reach: a height you can get to, and a thing you can get hold of.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种「够得到」：能达到的高度，以及能拿到手的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar set just within the reach of your hand
core.cn: 核心意象：横杆设在伸手就能碰到的高度

branches.en: A daily page target one can meet.
branches.cn: 能完成的每日页数目标。

branches.en: A bar lowered to a reachable height.
Free childcare only in a few districts.
branches.cn: 只在少数区能获得的免费托育。

branches.en: A salary one can earn in two years.

branches.cn: 两者都在现实限制之内。

intro.en: Attainable is at- plus tain plus -able; the same tain root builds contain, retain and maintain.
intro.cn: attainable 是 at- 加 tain 加 -able；同一 tain 词根还构成 contain、retain 与 maintain。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tangere, to touch, and attingere, to touch upon; tenere, to hold, gives the look-alike tain family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tangere「触」与 attingere「触及」；tenere「持」则给出形近的 tain 词族。

definition_zh: 达到；取得；抵达；成就；学识；造诣；学业成绩；达标指标
definition_en: the act of reaching or obtaining something through effort, and the achievement or level that results from it
core_image: 攀岩者的指尖终于触到岩壁顶端那条边——达到，就是努力伸长之后终于碰到目标的那一下
scene: 教育大臣举起一张图表，说我们只量得出成绩，却量不出孩子的好奇心。An education minister holds up a chart and says: We measure attainment, but a child's curiosity never appears on the chart.
sceneCN: 这里 attainment 先用「学业成绩、达到水平」（第 7 个义项：教育测量中的达到程度），再暗含「成就、素养」；句意：我们测量学业成绩，但孩子的好奇心从不出现在图表上。画面里有折线图、成绩单和一支教鞭。

pos.zh: 达到；取得；成就；学识；学业成绩

derivatives.zh: 无法达到的；高不可攀的

senses.title: The act of reaching
senses.titleCN: 达到：把努力伸到目标上
senses.definition: the act of reaching something that has been the object of effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力而触及某个目标的行为
senses.example: The attainment of fluency in a second language takes years of daily practice.
senses.exampleCN: 第二语言流利程度的达到需要多年每日练习。
senses.why: -ment names the act, as in movement and payment; attain goes back to ad- 'to' + tangere 'touch'. The act is imagined as contact: you do not merely want the goal, you stretch until you touch it.
senses.whyCN: -ment 像 movement、payment 一样把动词变成「行为」；attain 出自 ad-「向」+ tangere「触碰」。这个行为被想象成一次接触：不是只想要目标，而是一直伸到碰着它。

senses.title: Arriving at a place
senses.definition: the act of arriving at a place or at the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地或走完一段旅程的行为
senses.example: The attainment of the summit came after nine hours of climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 在攀登九个小时之后，他们抵达了顶峰。
senses.why: Latin attingere meant both 'to touch' and 'to arrive at': a ship touches shore, a climber touches rock. English kept the literal spatial sense beside the figurative one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 attingere 既指「触碰」，也指「到达」：船靠岸是 touch，登山者碰着岩壁也是 touch。英语把字面的空间义和比喻义一并保留下来。

senses.title: Making a goal real
senses.definition: the successful bringing about of a goal, standard, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 目标、标准或协议的顺利实现
senses.example: The attainment of the treaty took two years of quiet diplomacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约的达成用了两年安静的外交斡旋。
senses.why: The object of attaining can be abstract; a standard or an agreement is 'reached' once its conditions are met. The spatial metaphor is extended to anything with a threshold.
senses.whyCN: attain 的宾语可以是抽象物；标准或协议的条件一满足，就算「够到了」。这个空间比喻被推广到一切有门槛的事物。

senses.title: Obtaining a right or status
senses.definition: the obtaining of a right, qualification, or status, especially in formal use
senses.definitionCN: 权利、资格或身份的获得，尤用于正式语境
senses.example: Attainment of citizenship requires five years of residence.
senses.exampleCN: 取得公民身份需要居住满五年。
senses.why: Official English uses attainment for entering a status: citizenship, majority, a qualification. The status is treated as a place, and its conditions are the road that leads there.
senses.whyCN: 正式英语用 attainment 表示进入某种身份：公民资格、成年、资历。身份被当成一个地点，条件则是通往那里的路。

senses.title: A thing achieved
senses.titleCN: 成就：够下来的那件东西
senses.definition: an achievement or accomplishment, especially one won by sustained effort
senses.definitionCN: 尤指靠持续努力赢得的成就或业绩
senses.example: His greatest attainment was the bridge that still carries traffic today.
senses.exampleCN: 他最大的成就是那座至今仍在通车的桥。
senses.why: From the 1670s the noun also named the thing at the end of effort, not the effort itself. Since -ment can denote a result (as in 'a payment'), the touch became a possession.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 70 年代起，这个名词也指努力尽头的那件东西，而不只是努力本身。-ment 能表示结果（如 a payment），于是那一下触碰变成了一份所有物。

senses.title: Learned skill, usually plural
senses.titleCN: 学识：已经收进身体里的东西
senses.definition: a level of knowledge or skill in a subject, especially when impressive or scholarly
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科的知识或技能水平，尤指令人印象深刻或具学术性的
senses.example: She is a scholar of great attainments in medieval history.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位在中世纪史方面造诣很深的学者。
senses.why: The plural shifted the image from the act to the height reached: knowledge is what remains after the climb. The usage is slightly formal and old-fashioned, suited to praising a scholar.
senses.whyCN: 复数把意象从「动作」转到「达到的高度」：知识是攀登之后留在身上的东西。这种用法略正式、偏旧，适合称赞学者。

senses.title: Measured school level
senses.titleCN: 学业水平：把高度画成刻度
senses.definition: a pupil's measured level of knowledge, as recorded in school assessments
senses.definitionCN: 学生在学校评估中记录的知识水平
senses.example: Boys in the sample showed lower attainment in reading than girls.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中的男孩在阅读上表现出的学业水平低于女孩。
senses.why: Twentieth-century education made the height measurable: attainment became a score along a scale, used to compare groups. A metaphor of distance turned into a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的教育把这个高度变成可测量的东西：attainment 成了刻度上的分数，用来比较群体。距离的比喻由此变成统计数字。

senses.title: Attainment target
senses.titleCN: 达标指标：必须碰到的那条线
senses.definition: an official target set for pupils' or schools' results, used especially in British education
senses.definitionCN: 为学生或学校成绩设定的官方指标，尤用于英国教育
senses.example: The school narrowly missed its attainment target in mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以微弱差距未达到数学科的达标指标。
senses.why: British policy fixed 'attainment target' as an administrative phrase: the level a pupil or school is required to touch. The old image survives intact inside a government document.
senses.whyCN: 英国政策把 attainment target 固定为行政用语：学生或学校必须碰到的那条线。旧的意象原封不动地活在一份政府文件里。

senses.title: Something obtained
senses.titleCN: 取得物：努力留下的结果
senses.definition: something that has been obtained or brought into being as a result of effort
senses.definitionCN: 经努力而获得或产生的某物
senses.example: Clean water is an attainment that many villages still lack.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁的水是许多村庄至今仍未取得的一样东西。
senses.why: The result sense generalizes: anything brought into being by effort can be called an attainment, even an abstract good. Effort leaves a trace, and the trace takes the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 结果义进一步推广：任何靠努力产生的东西都能叫 attainment，哪怕是抽象的好事。努力留下痕迹，而这道痕迹沿用了动作的名字。

intro.en: Attainment is the noun of an old verb of touching. Latin tangere 'to touch' became attingere 'to reach by touching', French ataindre 'to reach', and English attain; the suffix -ment then turns the reaching into something nameable, countable and gradable.
intro.cn: attainment 是一个古老「触碰」动词的名词形式。拉丁语 tangere「触碰」变成 attingere「触而及之」，再变成法语 ataindre「达到」和英语 attain；后缀 -ment 又把「够到」变成可以命名、计数、评级的东西。

items.en: The root *tag- 'to touch, handle' is reconstructed from Latin tangere and its cognates. There is no written record of this layer, so it is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *tag-「触碰、摆弄」是从拉丁语 tangere 及其同源词重构出来的。这一层没有书面记录，因此标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Tangere 'to touch' formed attingere 'to touch; arrive at', from ad- 'to' + tangere. Latin already used the compound for 'attack, strike, manage', all felt as kinds of contact.
items.cn: tangere「触碰」构成 attingere「触及；到达」，由 ad-「向」+ tangere 组成。拉丁语已用它表示「攻击、打击、处理」，这些都被感受为不同方式的接触。

items.en: ataindre 'to come up to, reach, attain, strive' (Modern French atteindre) came from Vulgar Latin *attangere and supplied the stem ataign- that English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 ataindre「走近、达到、努力争取」（现代法语 atteindre）出自通俗拉丁语 *attangere，并提供了英语借入的词干 ataign-。

items.en: attain is recorded as 'succeed in reaching, come so near as to touch'. The borrowing belongs to the years around 1300, the period often described as the early 14th century.
items.cn: attain 被记录为「成功到达、近到可以触碰」。这一借入发生在 1300 年前后，也就是通常所说的 14 世纪初。

items.en: attainment enters through French atteignement as 'the action of acquiring by effort'. The suffix -ment names the act, as it does in payment and movement.
items.cn: attainment 经法语 atteignement 进入英语，意为「靠努力获取的行为」。后缀 -ment 命名动作，和 payment、movement 一样。

items.en: 'That which is attained, a personal accomplishment' is recorded from the 1670s. The plural attainments came to mean learned skill, and educational attainment and attainment target are 20th-century measurements.
items.cn: 「所达到之物、个人成就」记录于 17 世纪 70 年代。复数 attainments 后来指学术造诣，而 educational attainment 与 attainment target 是 20 世纪的测量用语。

note.en: The first group shares the -tainment ending or the tain/tang- root; the second group names results of effort that attainment can also denote.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -tainment 词尾或 tain/tang- 词根；第二组是 attainment 也能指称的各种努力成果。

entries.definition: to reach or obtain something by effort. It is the base of attainment, with the same tain/tang- root.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它是 attainment 的基础词，共享 tain/tang- 词根。

entries.definition: able to be reached or achieved. The -able suffix says the goal can be touched.
entries.definitionCN: 可达到的；可实现的。-able 后缀表示目标能够被够到。

entries.definition: the act of making amends, literally 'at-one-ment', from at + one. It is not related to attain.
entries.definitionCN: 赎罪；弥补，字面是 at-one-ment「成为一体」，由 at + one 构成，与 attain 不同源。

entries.definition: a reduction or lessening, from Old French abatre 'to beat down'. Only the -ment ending resembles attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；减少，出自古法语 abatre「打倒」。只有 -ment 词尾与 attainment 相似。

entries.definition: a thing accomplished by effort, especially something notable. It matches the 'thing achieved' sense of attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 成就；业绩。对应 attainment 的「成就」义。

entries.definition: the successful completion of a task, or a skill so gained. It stresses the finishing rather than the reaching.
entries.definitionCN: 完成；成就；才艺。它强调「完成」而非「够到」。

entries.definition: the act of obtaining something, especially knowledge or property. It fits the 'obtaining' sense of attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 获得；取得，尤指知识或财产。对应 attainment 的「取得」义。

entries.definition: the achievement of a desire, promise, or potential. It adds a sense of completeness to attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 实现；满足。它在 attainment 之上加了「圆满」的意味。

entries.definition: to arrive at or attain, or the distance one can stretch. It is the everyday word behind attainment's formal noun.
entries.definitionCN: 到达；够到；可及的距离。它是 attainment 这个正式名词背后的日常词。

normalIntro.en: The family is about contact: attain, contact, tangible and contagion all descend from Latin tangere 'to touch'.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族讲的是「接触」：attain、contact、tangible、contagion 都出自拉丁语 tangere「触碰」。

normal.en: at- 'to' + tain 'touch' + -ment: attainment is effort ending in contact.
normal.cn: at-「向」+ tain「触碰」+ -ment：attainment 就是努力以「碰上」收尾。

normal.en: Think of a target: an attainment target is the line a pupil must touch.
normal.cn: 想想靶子：attainment target 就是学生必须碰到的那条线。

normal.en: attain, contact and tangible all hide tangere, 'to touch'.
normal.cn: attain、contact、tangible 都藏着 tangere「触碰」。

normal.en: A person's attainments are the things already touched and kept — knowledge included.
normal.cn: 一个人的 attainments 是已经碰到并留下来的东西——包括知识。

normal.en: At the finish line the runner's hand touches the tape: that touch is the attainment.
normal.cn: 终点线上，跑者的手碰到绶带：那一下触碰就是 attainment。

abstract.en: The word always keeps a body in it: reaching is not wishing, it is extending until contact.
abstract.cn: 这个词里始终有一个身体：达到不是许愿，而是一直伸展到接触为止。

abstract.en: Act and result share one suffix: what you do and what you get are both -ment.
abstract.cn: 动作与结果共用一个后缀：你做的和你得的都是 -ment。

abstract.en: A school report measures a touch: how far a hand has stretched along a scale.
abstract.cn: 一份成绩单测量的是一次触碰：一只手沿刻度伸出了多远。

examples.en: The attainment of independence took decades of negotiation.
examples.cn: 独立的取得用了数十年的谈判。

examples.en: Her attainments in chemistry won her a place in the academy.
examples.cn: 她在化学上的造诣为她赢得了科学院的一席之地。

examples.en: The attainment gap between rich and poor pupils has widened.
examples.cn: 贫富学生之间的学业成绩差距扩大了。

dict_mnemonic.text: at（啊）+ tain（抬）+ ment（门）——啊，把东西抬到门楣上，终于够着了 → attainment 达到；成就

root: 源自拉丁语 attingere（ad-「向」+ tangere「触碰」）「触及、到达」，经古法语 ataindre 进入英语；核心是「努力伸长直到碰到目标」，再加 -ment 把这一动作及其结果名词化。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: reaching out until the fingers touch the goal. What is touched becomes an arrival, a right, an achievement, a body of learning, and finally a line on a school report.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个动作走：把手伸出去，直到指尖碰到目标。被碰到的可以是抵达、一项权利、一件成就、一身学问，最后变成成绩单上的一条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the hand stretching out and finally touching the goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：手一直伸出去，终于触到目标。

branches.en: THE ACT OF REACHING: effort making contact with a goal, whether a place, a standard or an agreement.
branches.cn: 达到的动作：努力与目标接触，无论目标是地点、标准还是协议。

branches.en: ARRIVAL: the literal touch of a shore, a summit or a finish line.
branches.cn: 抵达：字面地碰到海岸、山顶或终点线。

branches.en: OBTAINING: a right or status entered, and any thing left behind by effort.
branches.cn: 取得：进入某种权利或身份，以及努力留下的任何东西。

branches.en: WHAT IS WON: a single achievement, and the accumulated learning a person carries.
branches.cn: 所获：一件成就，以及一个人身上积累的学问。

branches.en: MEASURED HEIGHT: a score on a school scale and the official target line.
branches.cn: 被测出的高度：学校刻度上的分数，以及官方设定的目标线。

intro.en: attainment is at- (ad-, 'to') + tain (tang-, 'touch') + -ment (act or result noun). The same tang- root, worn down to -tain or -tact, runs through contact, contagion, tangible and tactile.
intro.cn: attainment 是 at-（ad-「向」）+ tain（tang-「触碰」）+ -ment（行为或结果名词）。同一个 tang- 词根磨成 -tain 或 -tact 后，贯穿 contact、contagion、tangible、tactile。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere 'to touch' yields attingere 'reach', contingere 'touch together' (whence contact), and tangibilis 'touchable'; its past participle tactus gives tactile.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere「触碰」给出 attingere「达到」、contingere「共同触及」（即 contact 的来源）和 tangibilis「可触的」；其过去分词 tactus 给出 tactile。

items.structure: at- (ad-, to) + tain (tang-, touch) + -ment (noun of act/result)
items.meaning: the act of reaching; an achievement or measured level
items.example: The attainment of a degree opened the door to research.
items.exampleCN: 取得学位为研究工作打开了大门。

items.meaning: to reach or achieve something by effort
items.example: Few runners attain that pace without years of training.
items.exampleCN: 没有多年训练，很少有跑者能达到那种配速。

items.example: Set an attainable goal for the first month.
items.exampleCN: 为第一个月设定一个可实现的目标。

items.meaningCN: 无法达到的；高不可攀的
items.example: Perfect fairness is an unattainable ideal.
items.exampleCN: 完全公平是一种无法达到的理想。

items.example: The report questions the attainability of the targets.
items.exampleCN: 报告质疑这些目标的可实现性。

items.meaning: the state of touching or communicating
items.example: The two plates meet at a point of contact.
items.exampleCN: 两块板在一个接触点相接。

items.meaning: the spreading of disease by contact
items.example: Doctors once blamed contagion on bad air.
items.exampleCN: 医生们曾把接触传染归咎于污浊的空气。

items.meaning: able to be passed on by contact
able to be touched, hence real and concrete
items.exampleCN: 这个项目产生了实实在在的成果。

items.meaning: not able to be touched; abstract

latinEntries.meaning: to touch; to handle; to reach
to touch; to arrive at; to attain

definition_zh: 试图；尝试；企图
definition_en: to try to do something difficult, or an act of trying
core_image: 伸手去够，指尖还差一点
scene: 他试着推开那扇卡住的门。He attempted to open the stuck door.
sceneCN: 这里 attempt 是「试图」（第 1 个义项：努力去做某事）；句意是他试图推开那扇卡住的门。

senses.title: Try to do something
senses.definition: to try to do something, especially something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 努力去做某事，尤其是困难的事
senses.example: He attempted to open the stuck door.
senses.exampleCN: 他试图推开那扇卡住的门。
senses.why: Attempt comes from Latin attemptare, from ad- 'to' and temptare 'to try or test', so it keeps the sense of reaching out to test whether a thing can be done.
senses.whyCN: attempt 源自拉丁语 attemptare，由 ad-「向」与 temptare「试、探」构成，保留着伸手试探某件事能否办成的意味。

senses.title: An act of trying
senses.definition: a single act of trying to do something
senses.definitionCN: 一次努力去做的行动
senses.example: Her first attempt failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一次尝试失败了。
senses.why: The same word works as a noun naming one round of effort, which is why attempts are counted and can be called first or failed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也作名词，指一轮努力，因此尝试可以计数，也能说第一次或失败的尝试。

intro.en: Attempt is a Latin word of testing, and a try is a reach made to see what happens.
intro.cn: attempt 是拉丁语中表示试探的词，一次尝试就是一次试探性的伸手。

items.en: temptare meant 'to try or test'.
items.cn: temptare 意为「尝试、试探」。

items.en: attemptare meant 'to try to reach'.
items.cn: attemptare 意为「试着够到」。

items.en: atempter meant 'to attempt or risk'.
items.cn: atempter 意为「尝试、冒险」。

items.en: English attempt covered both the effort and the risk.
items.cn: 英语 attempt 兼指努力与冒险。

items.en: The noun use settled for one round of effort.
items.cn: 名词用法固定为一轮努力。

note.en: The look-alike group is the tempt family; the near-meaning group gives other words for trying.
note.cn: 形近组是 tempt 词族；近义组是其他表示尝试的词。

normalIntro.en: An attempt is a reach whose result is still unknown.
normalIntro.cn: attempt 是一次结果尚未可知的伸手。

normal.en: The verb pattern is attempt to do, not attempt doing.
normal.cn: 动词结构是 attempt to do。

normal.en: As a noun it is countable: an attempt, three attempts.
normal.cn: 作名词可数：一次尝试、三次尝试。

normal.en: In an attempt to introduces a purpose.
normal.cn: in an attempt to 引出目的。

normal.en: Attempt is more formal than try.
normal.cn: attempt 比 try 正式。

normal.en: The final pt is pronounced as a clear t.
normal.cn: 词尾的 pt 读作清晰的 t。

abstract.en: See fingers an inch short of the handle.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖离把手还差一点。

abstract.en: See a door pushed once and then again.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被推了一次又一次。

abstract.en: See a mark on a wall counting failed tries.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上记着一次次失败的刻痕。

examples.en: He attempted to open the stuck door.
examples.cn: 他试图推开那扇卡住的门。

examples.en: Her first attempt failed.
examples.cn: 她的第一次尝试失败了。

examples.en: They made no attempt to hide the mistake.
examples.cn: 他们没有试图掩盖这个错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tempt（试探）：向目标伸手试一试，就是试图；试的这一轮，就是一次尝试。

root: 源自拉丁语 attemptare「试着够到」，由 ad-「向」与 temptare「尝试、试探」构成，经古法语 atempter 进入英语；动词指努力去做，名词指一轮尝试。

sensesIntro.en: The act of trying and one round of it share a single word.
sensesIntro.cn: 试着去做的动作与其中的一轮，共用同一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stretched out and not yet arriving.
core.cn: 核心意象：手伸出去，还没够到。

intro.en: The tempt root, 'to try', also gives temptation and tempt.
intro.cn: 词根 tempt 意为「试探」，也构成 temptation 与 tempt。

latinIntro.en: Latin temptare meant to test, and testing someone's will became tempting them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 temptare 意为试探，试探一个人的意志就变成了引诱。

definition_zh: 出席；照料；处理
definition_en: to be present at an event, or to take care of someone or something
core_image: 服务员侧身站在桌边，等你开口
scene: 会议室里坐满了人。Two hundred people attended the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 attend 是「出席」（第 1 个义项：到场参加）；句意是两百人出席了会议。

senses.title: Be present at
senses.definition: to be present at an event, school or meeting
senses.definitionCN: 到场参加活动、课程或会议
senses.example: Two hundred people attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 两百人出席了会议。
senses.why: Attend comes from Latin attendere, 'to stretch the mind toward', so presence began as directing one's attention to a place and then came to mean being there.
senses.whyCN: attend 源自拉丁语 attendere「把心思伸向」，所以「到场」最初是把注意力投向某处，后来才指人真的在那里。

senses.title: Take care of
senses.definition: to deal with or care for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人，或着手处理某事
senses.example: A nurse attended to the injured man.
senses.exampleCN: 一名护士照料那位受伤的男子。
senses.why: The same stretching of mind toward a person becomes nursing, and toward a problem becomes dealing with it, which is why attend takes the preposition to here.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「把心力伸向」用在人身上就是照看，用在事情上就是着手处理，因此这个义项要接介词 to。

intro.en: Attend is a word about stretching the mind toward something.
intro.cn: attend 是一个把心思伸向某物的词。

items.en: tendere meant 'to stretch'.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展」。

items.en: attendere meant 'to stretch the mind toward'.
items.cn: attendere 意为「把心思伸向」。

items.en: atendre meant 'to wait for or expect'.
items.cn: atendre 意为「等待、期待」。

items.en: English attend covered waiting on and being present.
items.cn: 英语 attend 兼指侍候与到场。

items.en: Attendance at events became the leading sense.
items.cn: 「出席活动」成为主要义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the tend family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of presence and care.
note.cn: 形近组是 tend 词族；近义组是表示到场与照料的动词。

normalIntro.en: Attend first meant to lean your mind toward, then to show up in person.
normalIntro.cn: attend 先指把心思倾过去，后指人亲自到场。

normal.en: For events, attend takes a direct object: attend a meeting.
normal.cn: 指参加活动时直接带宾语：出席会议。

normal.en: For care or problems, use attend to.
normal.cn: 指照料或处理时用 attend to。

normal.en: The double t comes from ad- plus tendere.
normal.cn: 双 t 来自 ad- 与 tendere 的结合。

normal.en: The noun is attendance, not attend.
normal.cn: 名词是 attendance。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TEND.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a whole row of chairs filled before the speaker begins.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲开始前整排椅子都坐满。

abstract.en: See a nurse turning toward a call bell.
abstract.cn: 想象护士转身走向呼叫铃。

abstract.en: See a head leaning slightly toward a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象脑袋微微倾向说话的声音。

examples.en: Two hundred people attended the meeting.
examples.cn: 两百人出席了会议。

examples.en: A nurse attended to the injured man.
examples.cn: 一名护士照料那位受伤的男子。

examples.en: She attends a language class twice a week.
examples.cn: 她每周上两次语言课。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tend（伸）：把心思伸向某处，是人到场；把心力伸向某人，是照看；伸向问题，是处理。

root: 源自拉丁语 attendere「把心思伸向」，由 ad-「向」与 tendere「伸」构成，经古法语 atendre 进入英语；由专注、侍候引申为到场出席。

sensesIntro.en: Presence, care and handling are three ways of stretching toward something.
sensesIntro.cn: 到场、照看与处理，是同一个「伸向」的三种落点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind leaning toward a point.
core.cn: 核心意象：心思向一个点倾过去。

intro.en: The tend root, 'to stretch', also gives extend, intend and tension.
intro.cn: 词根 tend 意为「伸」，也构成 extend、intend 与 tension。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere is the base, and its compounds fill English with reaching words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 是词基，其复合词让英语充满「伸展」类的词。

items.meaning: to stretch the mind to a plan
to lean or take care of

definition_zh: 出席；到场；出席人数；出勤情况；随侍
definition_en: the fact of being present at an event or place, the number present, and the record or duty of being there
core_image: 礼堂门口的签到簿：一排名字后面打了勾，几个空格格外扎眼
scene: 礼堂门口的桌上一本签到簿摊开着，多数名字后面打了勾，几个空格格外扎眼，讲台那边的灯已经亮起。Attendance at the lecture fell sharply after the midterm.
sceneCN: 这里指「出席人数」（第 2 个义项：到场者的数量）；句意为期中考试之后讲座的到场人数明显下降。图中可辨识物件：签到簿、打勾的笔迹、空白的格子、讲台灯。

pos.zh: 出席人数（可数或不可数）
随侍人员（古旧用法，可数）

senses.title: The act of being present
senses.definition: the fact of being present at a class, meeting or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在课程、会议或典礼上到场这一事实
senses.example: Her attendance at every rehearsal impressed the director.
senses.exampleCN: 她每次排练都到场，让导演印象深刻。
senses.why: the noun of action from the verb names the state of having stretched toward a place and stayed there.
senses.whyCN: 由动词派生的动作名词，指「朝某处伸身并留在那里」的状态。

senses.title: The number present
senses.definition: the count of people present at an event
senses.definitionCN: 到某场活动的人数
senses.example: Attendance at the lecture fell sharply after the midterm.
senses.exampleCN: 期中考试之后讲座的到场人数明显下降。
senses.why: the same noun slid from the act to the people performing it, then to their number.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从动作滑到做这个动作的人，再滑到这些人的人数。

senses.title: The habit of showing up
senses.titleCN: 出勤情况；是否经常到场
senses.definition: the pattern of being present regularly, judged as good or poor
senses.definitionCN: 是否经常到场的状态，被判断为良好或糟糕
senses.example: Regular attendance is required for the laboratory sessions.
senses.exampleCN: 实验课要求经常到场。
senses.why: schools and employers judge the pattern rather than a single occasion, so the word gained a qualitative reading.
senses.whyCN: 学校与雇主判断的是模式而非单次，于是这个词获得质量评价义。

senses.title: The measured rate
senses.definition: the proportion of possible occasions on which a person was present
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在本该到场的场合中实际到场的比例
senses.example: Attendance in the evening classes improved to eighty percent.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间课程的出勤率提高到八成。
senses.why: statistics added a denominator, turning a bare count into a rate without changing the core image.
senses.whyCN: 统计补上分母，把单纯的人数变成比率，核心意象未变。

senses.title: The record of presence
senses.definition: the sheet, book or file that records who was present
senses.definitionCN: 记录谁曾到场的表格、簿册或档案
senses.example: The attendance was checked against the sign-in sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 考勤记录与签到表做了核对。
senses.why: metonymy again: the act of being present, then the paper that proves it.
senses.whyCN: 仍是转喻：先是到场这一动作，再是证明它的那张纸。

senses.title: A body of attendants
senses.titleCN: 随行人员；侍从（古旧用法）
senses.definition: a group of people accompanying a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 随同显贵出行的一群人
senses.example: The duke traveled with a large attendance.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵出行带着一大群随从。
senses.why: the older sense of 'waiting upon' survives here: those who attend a person form a body around him.
senses.whyCN: 「侍奉」的旧义留在这里：侍奉某人的人在他周围形成一个群体。

senses.title: Care given to a person
senses.titleCN: 照料；看护（正式或古旧用法）
senses.definition: the service of looking after someone, especially a patient
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人、尤指病人的服务
senses.example: The patient needs constant medical attendance.
senses.exampleCN: 这名病人需要持续的医疗照护。
senses.why: looking after someone is a prolonged stretching of attention toward them, so the same noun covers care.
senses.whyCN: 照料某人是把注意力长期伸向对方，因此同一个名词也覆盖看护。

senses.title: The duty to appear
senses.titleCN: 到场义务；到庭义务（法律语境）
senses.definition: the legal obligation to be present when required, as at a court
senses.definitionCN: 在被要求时必须到场的法律义务，如到庭
senses.example: The witness's attendance was compelled by subpoena.
senses.exampleCN: 证人的到庭由传票强制。
senses.why: law turned presence into a duty, so the noun now names something one can be ordered to perform.
senses.whyCN: 法律把到场变成义务，于是这个名词指一种可被命令履行的事。

intro.en: Attendance comes from the verb attend, which English took from Old French atendre, itself from Latin attendere 'to stretch toward'.
intro.cn: attendance 来自动词 attend，英语经古法语 atendre 引入，后者出自拉丁 attendere「朝……伸展」。

items.en: Tendere meant 'to stretch, to extend', and it stands behind a large family of English verbs.
items.cn: 拉丁 tendere 意为「伸展、拉开」，英语一大串动词都由它派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus tendere produced attendere, to stretch one's mind or body toward something.
items.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀加 tendere 构成 attendere，即把心神或身体朝某物伸过去。

items.en: Old French atendre kept both the physical and the mental readings, including the sense of waiting for someone.
items.cn: 古法语 atendre 保留了身体与心神两读，还包括「等候某人」的意思。

items.en: English attend arrived in the fourteenth century and settled into 'be present at' and 'look after'.
items.cn: 英语 attend 在十四世纪进入，稳定为「到场」与「照料」两义。

items.en: The noun of action appeared soon after and took over the abstract senses: presence, turnout, care and duty.
items.cn: 动作名词随后出现，承接抽象义：到场、人数、照料与义务。

items.en: Dating note: the earliest noun citations are approximate, and the shift from 'waiting upon' to 'being present' cannot be dated to a single point.
items.cn: 年代说明：该名词最早书证只是约数；从「侍奉」到「到场」的转变无法锁定在某一时点。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same stretching root; group two holds other measures of being there.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「伸展」词根、容易看错的词；第二组是其他衡量「在场」的说法。

entries.definition: The verb of being present or looking after; the noun names the fact, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示到场或照料的动词；名词指事实，动词指动作。

entries.definition: A person who serves or accompanies; it is the human counterpart of the abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 提供服务或随行的人；是抽象名词的人形对应。

entries.definition: The same root applied to the mind rather than the body; it names concentration, not presence.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根用在对心神而非身体上；它指专注，而非到场。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who concentrates on another person; it describes attention, not turnout.
entries.definitionCN: 形容专注听某人的形容词；描述注意力，而非出席人数。

entries.definition: A plainer word for being in a place; it carries no count and no rate.
entries.definitionCN: 更朴素的说法，仅指在某处；不携带人数与比率。

entries.definition: The number who come to a vote, show or event; close to the count sense but more journalistic.
entries.definitionCN: 来参加投票、演出或活动的人数；接近人数义，但更像新闻用语。

entries.definition: Being involved in an activity rather than merely present; a silent attender may not participate.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动而非仅仅到场；默默到场者未必参与。

entries.definition: The habit of not being present; it measures the gaps the attendance record leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 不到场的习惯；它衡量的正是考勤记录留下的空格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real school phrases and real registers.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、真实校园说法与真实签到簿。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'toward' plus a verb meaning 'stretch': to stretch toward a place and stay there.
normal.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀加表示「伸展」的词根：朝某处伸身并停在那里。

normal.en: The verb gives the doing, the noun gives the fact, the count, the record and the duty.
normal.cn: 动词给动作，名词给事实、人数、记录与义务。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: take attendance, attendance record, regular attendance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：点名、出勤记录、经常出席。

normal.en: The same root builds attention, which stretches the mind instead of the body.
normal.cn: 同一词根还构成「注意」，只是把心神而非身体伸出去。

normal.en: Sister nouns measure the other side: absence and absenteeism.
normal.cn: 姊妹名词量的是另一面：缺席与旷工。

abstract.en: Picture a row of hooks by the door, each hook holding a name tag that was taken down.
abstract.cn: 想象门边一排挂钩，每个钩子上挂着一枚被取下的名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that only appears when someone stands in the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一道只在有人站进光里时才出现的影子。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge of stretched rope: presence is the rope held taut.
abstract.cn: 想象一座拉紧的绳索桥：到场就是绳子被拉紧的状态。

examples.en: Attendance at the lecture fell sharply after the midterm.
examples.cn: 期中考试之后讲座的到场人数明显下降。

examples.en: Regular attendance is required for the laboratory sessions.
examples.cn: 实验课要求经常到场。

examples.en: The witness's attendance was compelled by subpoena.
examples.cn: 证人的到庭由传票强制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝那里伸身」再加名词尾：人到了那里，就是出席

root: 由动词 attend 加名词词尾 -ance 构成；attend 出自拉丁 attendere，即表示「朝向」的前缀加 tendere「伸展」，原义为把心神或身体朝某物伸过去。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses follow presence itself: the act, the people, the habit, the rate, the record, the retinue, the care and the legal duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「在场」本身展开：动作、人、习惯、比率、记录、随从、照料与法律义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name tag taken from a hook by the door and put back when the person leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：门边挂钩上的名牌被取下，等人离开时又挂回去。

branches.en: ACT AND PEOPLE: presence itself, then everyone who is present.
branches.cn: 动作与人：先是在场本身，再是所有在场的人。

branches.en: HABIT AND RATE: the pattern judged, then the pattern expressed as a percentage.
branches.cn: 习惯与比率：先判断模式，再把模式写成百分比。

branches.en: PAPER PROOF: the sheet that turns presence into evidence.
branches.cn: 纸面证据：把在场变成证据的那张表。

branches.en: SERVICE SIDE: those who wait upon a person, and the care they give.
branches.cn: 侍奉一侧：随侍某人的人，以及他们提供的照料。

branches.en: LEGAL DUTY: presence ordered rather than offered.
branches.cn: 法律义务：到场出自命令，而非自愿。

intro.en: Attendance is a prefix, a root and a noun ending; the same pieces build the verb, the person, the mental noun and the legal duty.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、词根与名词词尾构成；同样的部件还构成动词、人物名词、心智名词与法律义务。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere 'to stretch' gives attend, attention, intend, extend and tension; ad- adds direction toward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tendere「伸展」衍生出 attend、attention、intend、extend 与 tension；表示「朝向」的前缀补出方向。

items.example: The prefix points the stretching toward an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「伸展」指向某个对象。

items.example: The root supplies the physical picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供具体的动作画面。

items.meaning: the state or act of doing
items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成状态的名词。

items.meaning: to be present at; to look after

items.example: Attendance is taken at the door.
The lecture held the audience's attention.
items.exampleCN: 讲座吸引了听众的注意。

items.meaning: the habit of not being present
items.example: Absenteeism falls when shifts are flexible.
items.exampleCN: 班次灵活时旷工率下降。

definition_zh: n. 服务员；看管人员；随从；adj. 伴随而来的；随之发生的
definition_en: A person whose job is to look after a place or serve customers; as an adjective, accompanying something as a result or circumstance.
core_image: 站在旁边随时准备接手的那个人
scene: 停车场的看管员在入口亭里抬手示意司机往前开。The parking attendant lifted a hand to wave the driver forward.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attendant 指在某个场所负责看管或服务的人员。

senses.title: A person who serves or watches
senses.definition: someone employed to look after a place, help customers or keep order
senses.definitionCN: 受雇看管场所、帮助顾客或维持秩序的人
senses.example: The lift attendant checked every floor.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯服务员逐层检查。
senses.why: Attend once meant to wait upon someone, so the -ant ending names the person doing that waiting.
senses.whyCN: attend 早期意为「侍候某人」，因此加 -ant 就指做这种侍候工作的人。

senses.title: An accompanying result
senses.definition: as an adjective, going along with something as a natural consequence or circumstance
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指作为自然结果或情形伴随某事而来
senses.example: They discussed the surgery and its attendant risks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们讨论了手术及随之而来的风险。
senses.why: The person sense is one who stands beside; the adjective keeps only the standing beside, applied to abstract things.
senses.whyCN: 人的义项是「站在旁边的人」；形容词只保留「站在旁边」，用来修饰抽象事物。

senses.title: A follower in a retinue
senses.definition: in older or formal use, a companion or servant travelling with a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时或正式用法中，指随同显贵出行的同伴或仆从
senses.example: The bishop arrived with two attendants.
senses.exampleCN: 主教带着两名随从抵达。
senses.why: Court language kept the waiting sense alive as a noun for the people who formed the train of a great person.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷语言把「侍候」义保留下来，用来指组成显贵随行队伍的人。

intro.en: Attendant is attend plus -ant; attend comes from Old French atendre, to wait for, from Latin attendere, to stretch towards, from ad-, to, and tendere, to stretch.
intro.cn: attendant 是 attend 加 -ant；attend 来自古法语 atendre「等待」，出自拉丁语 attendere「朝向伸展」，由 ad-「向」与 tendere「伸展」构成。

items.en: The root ten- meant to stretch, the reaching of attention towards something.
items.cn: 词根 ten- 意为「伸展」，即注意力朝某物伸过去。

items.en: Latin tendere meant to stretch or direct, the source of tend and extend.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为「伸展、指向」，是 tend 与 extend 的来源。

items.en: With ad-, to, it became attendere, to stretch towards, hence to give heed.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」成为 attendere「朝……伸展」，进而指「留意」。

items.en: Old French atendre meant to wait for, which shifted stretch into waiting.
items.cn: 古法语 atendre 意为「等待」，把「伸展」转成了「等候」。

items.en: Middle English took the French present participle as attendaunt, one who waits upon another.
items.cn: 中古英语借入法语现在分词作 attendaunt，指侍候他人的人。

items.en: By the fifteenth century attendant named a servant and, later, anything accompanying.
items.cn: 到十五世纪 attendant 既指仆从，后来又指任何伴随之物。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the attend family and one other -ant noun; the near-meaning group lists people who serve and one adjective of accompaniment.
note.cn: 形近组保留 attend 词族和另一个 -ant 名词；近义组列出服务人员和表示伴随的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who helps in work.
A servant on a ship or plane.
One who looks after a building.

normalIntro.en: Attendant is attend plus -ant: the one who attends, or the thing that attends upon an event.
normalIntro.cn: attendant 是 attend 加 -ant：侍候的人，或伴随某事而来的东西。

normal.en: Flight attendant is the commonest job title.
normal.cn: flight attendant 是最常见的职业名称。

normal.en: The adjective sits before risks or problems.
normal.cn: 形容词用法常放在 risks 或 problems 之前。

normal.en: -ant names a person; -ance names the act.
normal.cn: -ant 指人，-ance 指行为。

normal.en: Attendance is the act, attendant is the person.
normal.cn: attendance 是行为，attendant 是人。

normal.en: Attendant circumstances is a set legal phrase.
normal.cn: attendant circumstances 是固定法律用语。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing at a booth, ready.
abstract.cn: 想象有人站在亭子里随时待命。

abstract.en: Imagine a shadow that follows every decision.
abstract.cn: 想象一道跟着每个决定的影子。

abstract.en: Think of a train of people behind a bishop.
abstract.cn: 想象主教身后的一列随员。

examples.en: Ask the attendant for a locker key.
examples.cn: 向服务员要一把储物柜钥匙。

examples.en: Growth brings attendant pressures on housing.
examples.cn: 增长给住房带来随之而来的压力。

examples.en: Two attendants carried the ceremonial lamps.
examples.cn: 两名随从捧着仪仗灯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：attend「侍候、照料」+ -ant「做……的人」——在旁边照料的人就是 attendant。

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」加 ad-「向」成 attendere「把注意力伸向」，古法语 atendre 转为「等待、侍候」；加 -ant 指人，即 attendant，形容词保留「伴随」义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses keep the same picture of standing beside: a worker beside you, a result beside an event, a servant beside a lord.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都保留「站在旁边」这幅画面：身旁的服务员、事件旁的结果、显贵旁的随从。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone standing at your elbow, ready to take over
core.cn: 核心意象：站在你手边随时准备接手的那个人

branches.en: A booth keeper waving cars forward.
branches.cn: 在亭中示意车辆前行的看管员。

branches.en: A lift worker checking each floor.
branches.cn: 逐层检查的电梯服务员。

branches.en: Risks that come with the surgery.
Both name a person who waits upon another.
branches.cn: 两者都指侍候他人的人。

intro.en: Attendant is at- plus tend plus -ant; the tend root also builds attend, extend, intend and tension.
intro.cn: attendant 是 at- 加 tend 加 -ant；tend 词根还构成 attend、extend、intend 与 tension。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tendere, to stretch, attendere, to give heed, and tensio, a stretching; the -ant ending is the Latin present participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tendere「伸展」、attendere「留意」与 tensio「张力」；-ant 词尾就是拉丁语现在分词。

definition_zh: 注意；注意力；照料
definition_en: the act of focusing the mind on something, or practical care
core_image: 整间屋子的目光都落在同一处
scene: 老师敲了敲桌子。The class gave the teacher their full attention.
sceneCN: 这里 attention 是「注意力」（第 1 个义项：心思集中到某处）；句意是全班把注意力完全集中在老师身上。

senses.title: Focus of the mind
senses.definition: the act of directing your mind toward something
senses.definitionCN: 把心思集中到某件事上
senses.example: The class gave the teacher their full attention.
senses.exampleCN: 全班把注意力完全集中在老师身上。
senses.why: Attention is attend plus -tion, so the stretching of the mind toward a thing becomes the focus itself, something a speaker can ask a room to give.
senses.whyCN: attention 是 attend 加 -tion，把「心思伸向某处」变成那份专注本身，所以老师可以要求全班把它交出来。

senses.title: Practical care
senses.definition: care or treatment given to a person or problem
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人或某问题的照护与处置
senses.example: The patient needs immediate medical attention.
senses.exampleCN: 这名病人需要立即接受医疗照护。
senses.why: When the mind leans toward someone in need, the focus turns into hands-on care, which is why hospitals speak of medical attention.
senses.whyCN: 当心思倾向有需要的人时，专注就变成了实际动手的照护，所以医院会说医疗照护。

intro.en: Attention is the noun of stretching the mind, formed on the verb attend.
intro.cn: attention 是把心思伸出去的名词，由动词 attend 构成。

items.en: tendere meant 'to stretch'.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展」。

items.en: attendere meant 'to stretch the mind toward'.
items.cn: attendere 意为「把心思伸向」。

items.en: attentio meant 'a stretching toward'.
items.cn: attentio 意为「向某处的伸展」。

items.en: English attention named heed and care.
items.cn: 英语 attention 指留心与照看。

items.en: Psychology made attention a central term.
items.cn: 心理学使 attention 成为核心术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the attent stem; the near-meaning group names focus and care.
note.cn: 形近组共享 attent 词干；近义组是表示专注与照料的词。

entries.definition: to be present or care for

normalIntro.en: Attention is a stretch of the mind that can also become a helping hand.
normalIntro.cn: attention 是心思的一次伸展，也可以变成伸出的援手。

normal.en: It is uncountable in the focusing sense: pay attention.
normal.cn: 表示专注时不可数：pay attention。

normal.en: The verb after the phrase is pay, not give, in the fixed idiom.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 pay attention，不说 give attention。

normal.en: Medical attention means treatment, not concern.
normal.cn: medical attention 指治疗，不是关心。

normal.en: The adjective is attentive, the adverb attentively.
normal.cn: 形容词是 attentive，副词是 attentively。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TEN-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See every face in a room turned the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人脸都朝同一个方向。

abstract.en: See a spotlight narrowed to one chair.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯收窄到一把椅子上。

abstract.en: See a hand already reaching for a first-aid box.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手已经伸向急救箱。

examples.en: The class gave the teacher their full attention.
examples.cn: 全班把注意力完全集中在老师身上。

examples.en: The patient needs immediate medical attention.
examples.cn: 这名病人需要立即接受医疗照护。

examples.en: A loud noise drew everyone's attention.
examples.cn: 一声巨响吸引了所有人的注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: attend（把心思伸向）加 -tion：心思伸出去，是注意力；心思落到需要的人身上，是照护。

root: 由 attend 加 -tion 构成；attend 源自拉丁语 attendere「把心思伸向」，因此 attention 既指专注，也指落到某人身上的实际照护。

sensesIntro.en: Attention can be a beam of focus or a hand of care.
sensesIntro.cn: attention 可以是一束专注的光，也可以是一只照护的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every eye turned to one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：所有目光转向同一点。

intro.en: The -tion ending turns the verb of stretching into the state of being focused.
intro.cn: 结尾 -tion 把表示伸展的动词变成专注的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin attendere and attentio supply the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 attendere 与 attentio 提供了整族词。

definition_zh: 专注的；留心的；殷勤的
definition_en: giving close heed to someone or something, and quick to notice what they need
core_image: 一张矮桌旁，主人不声不响地把客人面前的杯子续满，又把窗缝关上，客人还没觉得冷。
scene: 矮桌旁，主人不声不响地把客人面前的杯子续满，又起身把窗缝合上，客人还没觉得冷。The attentive host noticed the draught before anyone mentioned it.
sceneCN: 这里指留心照料他人需要、抢先察觉的（第 2 个义项：体贴周到的）；句意为这位殷勤的主人在任何人开口之前就察觉了穿堂风。

pos.zh: 专注的；留心的；殷勤周到的

derivatives.zh: 注意；注意力（由形容词回到拉丁动作名词，指被给出的那份留意）
留意；出席（同族动词，由「朝……伸展」转指「留意」与「到场」）
专注地（加副词词尾，由形容词转指动作方式）
专注；殷勤（加表性质的名词词尾，由形容词转指该性质）
不注意的；漫不经心的（加表否定的前缀，由「专注」转指「缺乏专注」）

senses.title: Listening or watching closely
senses.definition: paying close heed to what is being said, shown or performed
senses.definitionCN: 对正在说出、展示或表演的内容保持密切留意
senses.example: The audience was attentive through the whole second act.
senses.exampleCN: 整个第二幕，观众都很专注。
senses.why: The core of the word is the mind stretched toward an object, so the first sense is simply that stretch maintained.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把留意说成持续的状态，于是听与看成了守着的姿态。

senses.title: Considerate of others' needs
senses.definition: quick to notice and serve what another person wants or lacks
senses.definitionCN: 敏锐察觉并照料他人所缺所需的
senses.example: The attentive host noticed the draught before anyone mentioned it.
senses.exampleCN: 这位殷勤的主人在任何人开口之前就察觉了穿堂风。
senses.why: The same heed is turned on a person rather than a task, and the result is described as courtesy.
senses.whyCN: 把「转向」用在他人所需上，同一种姿态便由留意变成服侍。

senses.title: Careful about detail
senses.definition: taking care over small points that others might pass over
senses.definitionCN: 对他人可能略过的小处也认真处理
senses.example: The proofreader was attentive to every comma.
senses.exampleCN: 这位校对者对每个逗号都很留心。
senses.why: Small points are what heed catches first, so the adjective extends from people to details.
senses.whyCN: 小处正是留意最先捕捉的东西，形容词便由人延伸到细节。

senses.title: Alert to danger
senses.definition: watchful for a threat that may appear without warning
senses.definitionCN: 对可能毫无预警出现的威胁保持警戒
senses.example: The lookout stayed attentive to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 瞭望者一直留意着海平线。
senses.why: Watchfulness for a threat is the same reaching out, with the object changed from a task to a risk.
senses.whyCN: 警戒是把留意对准未来的威胁，姿态相同，对象换成危险。

senses.title: High in attentiveness as a trait
senses.definition: in psychology, describing a person whose default level of heed is high across situations
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指在各种情境下留意水平都偏高的人
senses.example: Attentive children in the study also slept more regularly.
senses.exampleCN: 研究中的专注儿童睡眠也更规律。
senses.why: Psychology moves the word from an act to a disposition, so it can be measured across time.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把形容词变成可测量的特质，一时之举便成了稳定水平。

senses.title: Assiduous in duty
senses.definition: formal use for steady diligence in service, office or ritual
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中指在服务、职务或礼仪上持续勤谨
senses.example: The attendant was attentive to every rule of the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 这位侍从对仪式的每一条规矩都谨守不怠。
senses.why: Formal service is heed sustained over time, which is why the word appears in oaths and rituals.
senses.whyCN: 正式的职务是把留意拉长成时间，所以这个词出现在誓言与礼仪里。

senses.title: Heeding advice
senses.definition: giving serious heed to advice, warning or instruction
senses.definitionCN: 对劝告、警告或指示给予认真留意
senses.example: She was attentive to her tutor's corrections.
senses.exampleCN: 她对导师的指正很留心。
senses.why: Advice is heard before it is followed, so heeding words is the same act as watching a scene.
senses.whyCN: 劝告先被听见才被遵从，所以听进话与看住场面是同一个动作。

senses.title: Responsive service
senses.definition: describing service that answers a need promptly and without being asked
senses.definitionCN: 形容无需索求便及时回应需要的服务
senses.example: The hotel is known for attentive service rather than for size.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆出名的是殷勤的照应，而非规模。
senses.why: The word can be applied to an organization, where the heed is a policy rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 未经索求便回应的服务，是把留意向外变成行动。

intro.en: Attentive is Medieval Latin attentivus, from attendere 'to stretch toward, heed', plus the adjective suffix -ive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: attentive 出自中世纪拉丁 attentivus，来自 attendere「朝……伸展、留意」，加形容词词尾构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tendere meant 'to stretch'. Its deeper root is reconstructed as a form meaning 'to stretch', and that form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展」。其更早词根被重构为一个意为「伸展」的形式，属重构形式。

items.en: Ad- 'toward' plus tendere gave attendere 'to stretch toward', hence to heed or to wait upon.
items.cn: 表「朝向」的前缀加 tendere 构成 attendere「朝……伸展」，因此指留意或侍奉。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed attentivus 'giving heed', adding the adjective suffix of tendency to the verb's participle stem.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁构成 attentivus「留意的」，在动词分词词干上加表倾向的形容词词尾。

items.en: The adjective entered English in the fifteenth century, first describing a person given to heeding, then a person courteous in service.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十五世纪进入英语，先形容惯于留意的人，再形容在服侍上殷勤的人。

items.en: Psychology and service writing gave the word its current range, from a measurable trait to the quality of a hotel's staff.
items.cn: 心理学与服务行业的写作给出它今天的范围：从一个可测量的特质，到旅馆员工的水准。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed, and the pre-Latin root of tendere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：没有确切的最早书证；tendere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of stretching toward; group two holds adjectives of watchfulness and courtesy.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「朝……伸展」这一动词的词形；第二组是表示警觉与殷勤的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the heed itself; the adjective describes the one who gives it.
entries.definitionCN: 指所给出的留意本身；形容词描述给出它的人。

entries.definition: The verb for heeding or being present; the adjective is the resulting quality of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指留意或出席的动词；形容词是人由此呈现的性质。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being attentive; it names what the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 指「专注、殷勤」这一性质的名词；它命名形容词所描述者。

entries.definition: Describes a person who fails to heed; it is the direct opposite and is common in school reports.
entries.definitionCN: 形容未能留意的人；是直接的反义，常用于学校评语。

entries.definition: Quick to notice what is there, especially details others miss; it stresses perception rather than service.
entries.definitionCN: 指敏锐察觉眼前之物，尤其是他人忽略的细节；强调知觉，而非服侍。

entries.definition: Careful not to inconvenience others; it stresses avoiding harm, while attentive stresses noticing needs.
entries.definitionCN: 指小心不使他人不便；强调避免造成困扰，而 attentive 强调察觉需要。

entries.definition: Watchful and ready to react, usually to a risk; it is sharper and more defensive than attentive.
entries.definitionCN: 指警觉并准备反应，通常针对风险；比 attentive 更锐利、更偏防备。

entries.definition: Persistently careful in work; it concerns sustained effort rather than the direction of heed.
entries.definitionCN: 指在工作中持续用心；关心的是持久的努力，而非留意所向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A verb of stretching toward plus a suffix of tendency: a person inclined to reach out and hold.
normal.cn: 表「朝……伸展」的动词加表倾向的词尾：一个倾向于伸出去并停住的人。

normal.en: The family runs attend, attention, attentively and inattentive, all from one Latin verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 attend、attention、attentively、inattentive，全出同一个拉丁动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the two directions: attentive to detail, attentive to someone's needs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两个方向：注重细节、留意某人的需要。

normal.en: A host and a lookout share the word: one watches for comfort, the other for danger.
normal.cn: 主人与瞭望者共用这个词：一个留意舒适，一个留意危险。

normal.en: Service writing uses the adjective for staff, where heed becomes policy rather than mood.
normal.cn: 服务行业的文字用它形容员工，此处的留意成了制度，而非心情。

abstract.en: Picture a cup refilled before the guest notices it is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子在客人察觉空之前就被续满。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing a window before anyone feels the draught.
abstract.cn: 想象在任何人觉得有风之前，一只手已把窗关上。

abstract.en: Picture a lookout who keeps the horizon in view while others talk below.
abstract.cn: 想象瞭望者一直看着海平线，而其他人在下面说话。

examples.en: An attentive reader notices what the paragraph does not say.
examples.cn: 专注的读者会注意到段落没有说出的部分。

examples.en: The staff were attentive without being intrusive.
examples.cn: 员工殷勤而不打扰。

examples.en: He remained attentive to every objection during the hearing.
examples.cn: 听证过程中他对每个反对意见都保持留意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝……伸展」+ 表倾向的词尾——心常常伸出去的人：对事是专注，对人是殷勤。

root: 中世纪拉丁 attentivus，来自 attendere「朝……伸展、留意」= 表「朝向」的前缀 + tendere「伸展」；tendere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one disposition: heed that reaches out and stays. Staying on a performance is close listening; staying on a person is courtesy; staying on small points is care over detail; staying on a horizon is vigilance; staying on everything is a trait; staying on a duty is assiduity; staying on advice is obedience to correction; and staying on a guest is service.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种倾向展开：伸出去并停住的留意。停在演出上是专注倾听；停在人身上是殷勤；停在小处是注重细节；停在海平线上是警觉；停在一切之上是稳定特质；停在职守上是勤谨；停在劝告上是听从指正；停在客人身上是照应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup refilled before the guest notices, and a window closed before anyone feels the draught.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子在客人察觉之前被续满，窗在任何人觉得有风之前被关上。

branches.en: THE HELD ATTENTION: close listening, and the same care spent on commas.
branches.cn: 被持住的注意：专注地听，与把同样的用心花在逗号上。

branches.en: COURTESY IN PERSON AND IN SERVICE: a host who notices, and a staff trained to notice.
branches.cn: 人身上的与制度里的殷勤：会察觉的主人，与被训练去察觉的员工。

branches.en: THE WATCH ON THE HORIZON: heed turned toward a risk that may come without warning.
branches.cn: 盯住海平线：留意转向可能毫无预警到来的风险。

branches.en: DUTY AND CORRECTION: steady diligence in office, and serious heed to advice.
branches.cn: 职守与指正：在职务上持续勤谨，与对劝告的认真留意。

branches.en: THE TRAIT BEHIND ALL OF THEM: a default level of heed that holds across situations.
branches.cn: 所有义项背后的特质：在各种情境下都偏高的留意水平。

intro.en: The adjective is one Latin verb of stretching with a prefix of direction and a suffix of tendency.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由一个表「伸展」的拉丁动词、一个表方向的前缀与一个表倾向的后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin attendere and its participle give attend, attention and attentive; the suffix -ivus gives the tendency adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 attendere 及其分词衍生 attend、attention、attentive；后缀 -ivus 构成表倾向的形容词。

items.example: The verb gave the family its image of reaching.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给整个词族「伸出」的形象。

items.example: The compound made direction into heed.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把方向变成留意。

items.example: Medieval Latin formed the adjective on the participle stem.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁在分词词干上构成这个形容词。

items.example: He attends to the smallest change.
She was attentive to the visitor's comfort.
Attentiveness is part of the job.
items.exampleCN: 殷勤是这份工作的一部分。

items.example: An inattentive driver missed the sign.
items.exampleCN: 一个不留神的司机错过了标牌。

definition_zh: n. 阁楼；屋顶正下方的顶层房间或空间
definition_en: A room or space just under the roof of a house, often used for storage.
core_image: 屋顶斜面下那间要低头走的小屋
scene: 他们在屋顶下那间小屋里翻出一只旧箱子。They found an old trunk in the attic under the sloping roof.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attic 指屋顶正下方、常用来堆放杂物的顶层空间。

senses.title: The space under the roof
senses.definition: the room or unfinished area directly beneath the roof of a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物屋顶正下方的房间或未装修区域
senses.example: The cases were stacked along the attic wall.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子沿着阁楼的墙堆放。
senses.why: The word came from Attic architecture, where a low storey was set above the main cornice, so the top space took the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自阿提卡式建筑：主檐口之上再加一层矮层，于是顶层空间就沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: A place for stored things
senses.definition: by extension, the part of a house where old possessions are put out of the way
senses.definitionCN: 引申指家中把旧物挪开存放的那一部分
senses.example: Her letters had lain in the attic for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信件在阁楼里躺了几十年。
senses.why: Because that space was cheap and awkward, it became the natural store, and the word carries the smell of dust and old boxes.
senses.whyCN: 因为那块空间廉价又不规整，它成了天然的储物处，这个词也带上了灰尘与旧箱子的气味。

intro.en: Attic is short for Attic storey, from Greek Attikos, of Attica, the region of Athens, whose builders set a small order above the main cornice.
intro.cn: attic 是 Attic storey「阿提卡层」的省略，出自希腊语 Attikos「阿提卡的」，即雅典所在地区，那里的工匠在主檐口之上再加一层小型柱式。

items.en: Attica was the district around Athens, and its name gave the adjective Attikos.
items.cn: 阿提卡是雅典周边地区，其名产生形容词 Attikos。

items.en: Attikos meant of Attica, and by extension elegant, since Athenian taste was the standard.
items.cn: Attikos 意为「阿提卡的」，并引申为「雅致的」，因为雅典品味被视为标准。

items.en: Latin took the word as Atticus, used for both Athenian style and a refined manner.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 Atticus，既指雅典风格，也指优雅的举止。

items.en: French architecture used attique for a low storey above the main cornice.
items.cn: 法国建筑用 attique 指主檐口之上的一层矮层。

items.en: English adopted attic storey in the eighteenth century, then shortened it to attic.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪采用 attic storey，随后缩略为 attic。

items.en: By the nineteenth century attic meant the whole room under the roof, not just the architectural feature.
items.cn: 到十九世纪 attic 指屋顶下的整个房间，而不再只指那个建筑构件。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words that share the opening letters; the near-meaning group lists other names for the top space of a house.
note.cn: 形近组保留开头字母相同的词；近义组列出房屋顶层空间的其他名称。

entries.definition: A diplomat on a mission staff.
To declare that something is true.
An upper space under a roof.
A tiny room at the top of a house.
A roof whose slope holds rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 斜面内可设房间的屋顶。

entries.definition: A small loft just under the ridge.

normalIntro.en: Attic began as Attic storey, a top layer in Athenian style, and now means the room under any roof.
normalIntro.cn: attic 起初是 Attic storey「雅典式顶层」，如今泛指任何屋顶下的房间。

normal.en: Say in the attic, not on the attic.
normal.cn: 要说 in the attic，不说 on the attic。

normal.en: An attic conversion turns storage into a room.
normal.cn: attic conversion 把储物空间改成房间。

normal.en: A loft is often open; an attic is usually closed.
normal.cn: loft 常是开敞的，attic 通常是封闭的。

normal.en: A garret is a poor little attic.
normal.cn: garret 是穷困的小阁楼。

normal.en: Capital Attic means Athenian, lower case means the room.
normal.cn: 大写 Attic 指雅典的，小写指阁楼。

abstract.en: Picture a sloping ceiling you must duck under.
abstract.cn: 想象一片必须低头才能走的斜天花板。

abstract.en: Imagine dust hanging in a single window beam.
abstract.cn: 想象灰尘悬在一道窗光里。

abstract.en: Think of a trunk that has not moved in years.
abstract.cn: 想象一只多年未动的箱子。

examples.en: They slept in a narrow attic room.
examples.cn: 他们睡在一间狭窄的阁楼房里。

examples.en: The attic was full of broken chairs.
examples.cn: 阁楼里堆满破损的椅子。

examples.en: A ladder led up to the attic hatch.
examples.cn: 一架梯子通向阁楼的舱口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：Attic「雅典式的」+ storey「楼层」——雅典式建筑在主檐口上加的那层矮楼，就是 attic 阁楼。

root: 希腊语 Attikos「阿提卡的、雅典式的」经拉丁语 Atticus、法语 attique 进入建筑术语，指主檐口之上的矮层 attic storey；缩略为 attic 后转指屋顶下的整个房间。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses point to the same place: the architectural space beneath the roof, and that space used as the house store for old things.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项指向同一处地方：屋顶之下的建筑空间，以及被当作旧物仓库使用的那个空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low room under a sloping roof where you must duck
core.cn: 核心意象：屋顶斜面下那间要低头走的小屋

branches.en: A room beneath the sloping roof.
A hatch reached by a ladder.

branches.cn: 数十年无人翻动的信件。

branches.en: The same space, seen as room and as store.
branches.cn: 同一空间，既作房间也作仓库。

intro.en: Attic is a place adjective turned noun: Attic plus storey; the same clipping pattern gives basement and mezzanine their everyday use.
intro.cn: attic 是地名形容词转为名词：Attic 加 storey；同样的省略方式也让 basement 与 mezzanine 进入日常用法。

latinIntro.en: The layer is Greek rather than Latin: Attikos, of Attica, passed through Latin Atticus; Greek oikos, house, gives economy beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这一层属希腊语而非拉丁语：Attikos「阿提卡的」经拉丁语 Atticus 传来；旁边的希腊语 oikos「房屋」产生 economy。

definition_zh: n. 服装；衣着（尤指正式或特定场合的）；v. 使穿戴；打扮
definition_en: Clothes, especially fine or formal ones worn for a particular occasion; as a verb, to dress someone in such clothes.
core_image: 为某个场合从头到脚配好的一身行头
scene: 请柬上写明要穿正式服装，她于是挑了那件深蓝长裙。The invitation said formal attire, so she chose the long navy dress.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attire 指为某个场合准备的整套衣着，语体偏正式。

senses.title: Clothes for an occasion
senses.definition: the clothes a person wears, thought of as a complete set suited to an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所穿的衣物，被视为适合某场合的一整套
senses.example: Guests were asked to wear evening attire.
senses.exampleCN: 来宾被要求穿晚礼服。
senses.why: Attire came from a verb meaning to put in order, so it names clothes as an arranged whole rather than single items.
senses.whyCN: attire 源自意为「整理妥当」的动词，因此它把衣着看作安排好的整体，而非单件衣物。

senses.title: To dress someone
senses.definition: as a verb, to put clothes on a person, usually in a formal or ceremonial way
senses.definitionCN: 作动词，指给人穿上衣服，通常带正式或礼仪色彩
senses.example: The bride was attired in white brocade.
senses.exampleCN: 新娘身穿白色织锦。
senses.why: The noun and verb grew together, so the passive be attired in is the natural verb pattern.
senses.whyCN: 名词与动词一同发展，因此被动式 be attired in 是最自然的动词句式。

senses.title: Dress that marks a group
senses.definition: a style of dress taken as the mark of a group, period or profession
senses.definitionCN: 被视为某群体、时代或职业标志的一种装束风格
senses.example: The painting records the attire of rural monks.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画记录了乡村僧侣的装束。
senses.why: Because attire already means an arranged whole, it slides easily into meaning the look that identifies a group.
senses.whyCN: 既然 attire 本就指安排好的整体，它便顺势用来指能标识某群体的整体外观。

intro.en: Attire is a- plus tire, an Old French word for rank or order; the verb atirier meant to put in order or equip, and the noun followed from it.
intro.cn: attire 是 a- 加 tire——古法语中表示「行列、次序」的词；动词 atirier 意为「整理妥当、装备」，名词由此产生。

items.en: A Germanic word for adornment or ordered gear stands behind the second half of the word.
items.cn: 一个意为「装饰、成套装备」的日耳曼词是这个词后半部分的来源。

items.en: Old French tire meant a rank or row, the notion of things set out in order.
items.cn: 古法语 tire 意为「行列、次序」，即把东西排列有序的概念。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave atirier, to put in order, to equip or adorn a person.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 atirier，意为「整理妥当、装备或打扮某人」。

items.en: Middle English atiren kept both equipping and dressing, and the noun followed from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 atiren 兼有「装备」与「穿衣」两义，名词随之产生。

items.en: By the fourteenth century attire was an ordinary formal word for the clothes a person wore.
items.cn: 到十四世纪 attire 已是指人衣着的常用正式词。

items.en: Today the noun survives mainly in dress codes, while the verb lives on in the passive.
items.cn: 今天名词主要保留在着装规定中，动词则以被动形式延续。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words that end in the same sound; the near-meaning group lists other words for a set of clothes.
note.cn: 形近组保留结尾读音相同的词；近义组列出表示成套衣着的其他词。

entries.definition: A set of clothes worn together.

normalIntro.en: Attire hides a- plus tire, an old word for order: clothes put in order for the occasion.
normalIntro.cn: attire 里藏着 a- 加 tire——tire 是表示「次序」的旧词：为场合整理妥当的一身衣服。

normal.en: Formal attire is the standard dress-code phrase.
normal.cn: formal attire 是着装规定的标准说法。

normal.en: The noun is uncountable in normal use.
normal.cn: 名词在常规用法中不可数。

normal.en: The verb appears as be attired in.
normal.cn: 动词常见形式是 be attired in。

normal.en: Attire is more formal than clothes.
normal.cn: attire 比 clothes 更正式。

normal.en: Business attire usually means a suit.
normal.cn: business attire 通常指西装。

abstract.en: Picture a whole outfit laid out on a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象一整套衣服摊在床上。

abstract.en: Imagine a robe placed on shoulders in a rite.
abstract.cn: 想象仪式中把长袍披上肩头。

abstract.en: Think of a painting read by its costumes.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅可以凭服饰读懂的画。

examples.en: The staff wore neat business attire.
examples.cn: 员工穿着整洁的商务服装。

examples.en: She was attired in a grey travelling cloak.
examples.cn: 她身穿灰色旅行斗篷。

examples.en: Ceremonial attire is kept in the vestry.
examples.cn: 礼仪服饰存放在圣器室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ tire「行列、次序」——把全身衣物按场合排妥当，就是 attire。

root: 古法语 tire「行列、次序」加 a-「向」成 atirier「整理、装备」，入中古英语作 atiren「打扮」；名词 attire 由「整理好的一身」转指服装。

sensesIntro.en: The senses share one idea of a set put in order: clothes chosen for an occasion, the act of putting them on, and the look that marks a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项共享「整理成套」这一想法：为场合挑好的衣服、把它们穿上的动作，以及标识某群体的整体外观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole outfit arranged head to foot for one occasion
core.cn: 核心意象：为某个场合从头到脚配好的一身行头

branches.en: A navy dress chosen for a formal card.
branches.cn: 为正式请柬挑的深蓝长裙。

branches.en: A bride dressed in white brocade.
Both treat clothes as one arranged whole.
branches.cn: 两者都把衣着视为安排好的整体。

intro.en: Attire is a- plus tire; the same a- prefix builds arise and awake, while the dress field supplies apparel and garment.
intro.cn: attire 是 a- 加 tire；同一 a- 前缀还构成 arise 与 awake，而服饰义场提供 apparel 与 garment。

latinIntro.en: The word is French rather than Latin: tire, order, and atirier, to equip; Latin ornare, to adorn, gives ornament beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属法语而非拉丁语层次：tire「次序」与 atirier「装备」；旁边拉丁语 ornare「装饰」产生 ornament。

latinEntries.example: Tire is the hidden half of attire.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tire 是 attire 隐藏的后半部分。

definition_zh: 态度；看法；姿势
definition_en: a way of thinking or feeling about something, or a bodily posture
core_image: 身体微微前倾，把立场写在姿态上
scene: 面试官问他对加班怎么看。His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
sceneCN: 这里 attitude 是「态度」（第 1 个义项：对事情的看法与姿态）；句意是他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。

senses.title: Way of thinking
senses.definition: a settled way of thinking or feeling about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事较为固定的想法与感受
senses.example: His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。
senses.why: Attitude came from Italian attitudine, 'aptness or posture', from Latin aptitudo 'fitness', so the mental sense grew out of a body set a certain way.
senses.whyCN: attitude 来自意大利语 attitudine「适宜、姿态」，其拉丁词源 aptitudo 意为「适合」，所以心里的看法是从身体的摆法长出来的。

senses.title: Bodily posture
senses.definition: a position in which the body is held
senses.definitionCN: 身体摆出的姿势
senses.example: He stood in an attitude of prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 他摆出祈祷的姿势站着。
senses.why: The oldest sense was the body's pose, and this concrete use survives in literary description even though the mental sense now dominates.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是身体的摆法，尽管如今心里的看法占主流，这个具体义仍保留在文学描写中。

intro.en: Attitude is a word of fitness that began with the body and moved into the mind.
intro.cn: attitude 本是个表示「适合」的词，从身体移到了心里。

items.en: aptus meant 'fit or suited'.
items.cn: aptus 意为「适合的」。

items.en: aptitudo meant 'fitness or posture'.
items.cn: aptitudo 意为「适合、姿态」。

items.en: attitudine meant 'a pose of the body'.
items.cn: attitudine 意为「身体的姿势」。

items.en: French attitude kept the painter's sense of a pose.
items.cn: 法语 attitude 保留画家所说的姿态义。

items.en: The mental sense of a view became dominant.
items.cn: 表示看法的心理义成为主流。

note.en: The look-alike group is easily confused in spelling; the near-meaning group names views and poses.
note.cn: 形近组拼写易混；近义组是表示看法与姿态的词。

entries.definition: a public position on an issue
the way the body is held

normalIntro.en: Attitude began as the body's pose and became the mind's pose.
normalIntro.cn: attitude 从身体的姿势变成心里的姿势。

normal.en: Use attitude to or towards for the object of a view.
normal.cn: 表示看法对象时用 attitude to 或 towards。

normal.en: The plural attitudes is common in surveys.
normal.cn: 调查中常用复数 attitudes。

normal.en: Strike an attitude means pose, often for effect.
normal.cn: strike an attitude 指摆姿势，常带做作意味。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with aptitude, which is ability.
normal.cn: 不要与 aptitude 混淆，后者是天资。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AT-ti-tude.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See shoulders squared before a difficult question.
abstract.cn: 想象难题来临前肩膀一挺。

abstract.en: See a model frozen in a painted pose.
abstract.cn: 想象模特定格在一个画中的姿势。

abstract.en: See a face that has already decided before the words come.
abstract.cn: 想象话还没出口，脸上的判断已经定了。

examples.en: His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
examples.cn: 他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。

examples.en: He stood in an attitude of prayer.
examples.cn: 他摆出祈祷的姿势站着。

examples.en: Public attitudes towards the plan have changed.
examples.cn: 公众对这项计划的态度已经改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: attitude 与 aptitude 同源，本义是「摆得合适的样子」：身体的摆法是姿势，心里的摆法是态度。

root: 源自拉丁语 aptitudo「适合、姿态」，经意大利语 attitudine 与法语进入英语；本指身体的姿势，后引申为心里对事物的固定看法。

sensesIntro.en: A pose of the body and a pose of the mind are the same word.
sensesIntro.cn: 身体的摆法与心里的摆法，是同一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body set at a slight angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体摆出一个微斜的角度。

intro.en: The -itude ending marks a noun of state, as in aptitude and solitude.
intro.cn: 结尾 -itude 表示状态名词，如 aptitude 与 solitude。

latinIntro.en: Latin aptus, 'fit', also gives apt and aptitude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aptus「适合」也是 apt 与 aptitude 的来源。

definition_zh: 律师；代理人
definition_en: a lawyer, or a person given legal power to act for another
core_image: 一个人被正式授权，替另一个人开口
scene: 法庭上被告身边坐着一位穿黑衣的人。Her attorney spoke for her in court.
sceneCN: 这里 attorney 是「律师」（第 1 个义项：受委托代理法律事务的人）；句意是她的律师在法庭上替她发言。

senses.title: Lawyer
senses.definition: a lawyer who is qualified to act for people in legal matters
senses.definitionCN: 有资格在法律事务中代表他人的律师
senses.example: Her attorney spoke for her in court.
senses.exampleCN: 她的律师在法庭上替她发言。
senses.why: Attorney comes from Old French atorner, 'to assign', so the attorney was first the one assigned to stand in another's place, and law kept that role as the courtroom lawyer.
senses.whyCN: attorney 来自古法语 atorner「指派」，本指被指派代替他人的人，法律沿用了这个角色，用它指法庭上的律师。

senses.title: Authorized agent
senses.definition: a person given legal power to act for someone else
senses.definitionCN: 获得法律授权、代替他人行事的人
senses.example: She acted as attorney for her elderly father.
senses.exampleCN: 她作为年迈父亲的代理人行事。
senses.why: The original sense of a person appointed to act in another's place survives in documents such as a power of attorney, where no courtroom is involved.
senses.whyCN: 「被指派代替他人行事」这个本义保留在授权书一类的文件里，那种场合与法庭无关。

intro.en: Attorney is a French word of appointment, and appointment still lies at its centre.
intro.cn: attorney 是法语中表示「指派」的词，指派至今仍是它的核心。

items.en: atorner meant 'to assign or arrange'.
items.cn: atorner 意为「指派、安排」。

items.en: atorne meant 'one appointed'.
items.cn: atorne 指「被指派的人」。

items.en: English attorney named a legal representative.
items.cn: 英语 attorney 指法律上的代表人。

items.en: Attorney at law became the courtroom lawyer.
items.cn: attorney at law 成为出庭律师的称呼。

items.en: Attorney became the ordinary word for lawyer.
items.cn: 在美国英语中，attorney 成为律师的常用说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the attorney stem; the near-meaning group names legal professionals.
note.cn: 形近组共享 attorney 词干；近义组是法律职业的称呼。

entries.definition: a legal adviser in a case

normalIntro.en: An attorney is someone appointed to speak in your place.
normalIntro.cn: attorney 是被指派到你位置上说话的人。

normal.en: The plural is attorneys, not attornies.
normal.cn: 复数是 attorneys。

normal.en: In the United States, attorney is the everyday word for lawyer.
normal.cn: 在美国英语里 attorney 就是日常说的律师。

normal.en: Power of attorney names the document, not the person.
normal.cn: power of attorney 指授权书，不指人。

normal.en: The word has a soft c sound in the middle? No, it has no c.
normal.cn: 词中并没有 c，注意不要按拼写误读。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TOR-ney.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a black robe standing at a courtroom table.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭桌边站着一位黑袍人。

abstract.en: See a signed paper granting someone a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一份签字文件把发言权交给别人。

abstract.en: See two chairs, one empty and one occupied by a representative.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子，一把空着，一把坐着代理人。

examples.en: Her attorney spoke for her in court.
examples.cn: 她的律师在法庭上替她发言。

examples.en: She acted as attorney for her elderly father.
examples.cn: 她作为年迈父亲的代理人行事。

examples.en: The company hired an attorney to review the contract.
examples.cn: 公司聘请了一名律师审阅合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 古法语 atorner 是「指派」：被指派到你的位置上说话的人，是律师；被授权替你处理事务的人，是代理人。

root: 源自古法语 atorner「指派、安排」，指被指派代替他人行事的人；进入英语后专指法律代表，在美国英语中成为律师的常用称呼。

sensesIntro.en: Courtroom advocate and authorized agent are two settings for one appointed role.
sensesIntro.cn: 法庭上的辩护人与授权代理人，是同一个被指派角色的两种场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seat occupied on another's behalf.
core.cn: 核心意象：替别人坐上的那个位置。

intro.en: Attorney is a borrowed whole word, but it anchors a small legal family.
intro.cn: attorney 是整体借入的词，但撑起了一个小型法律词族。

latinIntro.en: The French stem atorner goes back to Latin ordinaire, 'to arrange'.
latinIntro.cn: 法语词干 atorner 可追溯到拉丁语 ordinaire「安排」。

definition_zh: 吸引；引起（注意、兴趣）；招致（批评、麻烦）
definition_en: to pull someone or something toward a place, or to make people interested or notice something
core_image: 一块磁石把四周的铁屑都拉成一个小圈
scene: 夜市摊主把灯调亮，路过的人不由自主地靠近。The bright stall attracted a crowd within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 attract 是「吸引」（第 1 个义项：把人或物拉向自己）；句意是明亮的摊位几分钟内就吸引了一群人。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有吸引力的；好看的

senses.title: Draw near
senses.definition: to pull someone or something toward a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物拉向某处或某人
senses.example: The flowers attract bees in early summer.
senses.exampleCN: 初夏时这些花吸引蜜蜂。
senses.why: The Latin base trahere means 'to draw or pull', so the first sense is a physical pull, as a magnet draws iron.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 trahere 意为「拉、拖」，所以第一义项是物理意义上的拉近，像磁石把铁吸过来。

senses.title: Arouse interest
senses.definition: to make people interested in something or make them notice it
senses.definitionCN: 使人对某事物产生兴趣或注意到它
senses.example: The title attracted my attention at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标题立刻引起了我的注意。
senses.why: The pull moves from the body to the mind: eyes and curiosity are drawn toward the thing, though nothing physically moves.
senses.whyCN: 这种「拉」从身体转到心里：目光和好奇心被牵过去，物体本身并没有移动。

senses.title: Bring something bad
senses.definition: to cause something unpleasant to come to you
senses.definitionCN: 招来不愉快的事，如批评或麻烦
senses.example: His remarks attracted sharp criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他的言论招致尖锐的批评。
senses.why: Here the pull works in reverse: your own words or deeds draw consequences onto you, and those consequences are usually unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「拉」方向相反：自己的言行把后果拉到自己身上，而这类后果通常不受欢迎。

intro.en: Attract is built from a Latin verb meaning to draw something toward oneself.
intro.cn: attract 由拉丁语中表示「把东西拉向自己」的动词构成。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw, pull or drag'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖、牵引」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus trahere made attrahere, 'to draw to oneself'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 trahere 构成 attrahere，意为「拉向自己」。

items.en: The past participle attractus described something already drawn near.
items.cn: 过去分词 attractus 描述已被拉近的东西。

items.en: English attracten first meant to draw or allure.
items.cn: 中古英语 attracten 最初表示拉近或引诱。

items.en: The word widened to interest, appeal and unwanted consequences.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到引起兴趣、产生吸引力以及招致不良后果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root tract; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of drawing people in.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 tract；近义组是其他表示「把人拉过来」的动词。

entries.definition: to draw together and become smaller
to pull or pull in interest

normalIntro.en: Attract is a pull, first on things, then on eyes and minds.
normalIntro.cn: attract 是一种拉力，先拉物体，再拉目光和心思。

normal.en: The prefix at- is really ad-, meaning to.
normal.cn: 前缀 at- 其实是 ad-，意为「向」。

normal.en: Picture a magnet: whatever it draws is attracted.
normal.cn: 想象一块磁石：被它拉过来的东西就是被吸引的。
