normal.en: Attract attention and attract interest are the two everyday patterns.
normal.cn: attract attention 与 attract interest 是两个最常用的搭配。

normal.en: Attract criticism shows the same pull applied to bad results.
normal.cn: attract criticism 说明同一个「拉」也能用在糟糕的结果上。

normal.en: The noun is attraction and the adjective is attractive.
normal.cn: 名词是 attraction，形容词是 attractive。

abstract.en: See iron filings jump and cling to a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象铁屑跳起来，紧紧贴在磁石上。

abstract.en: See moths circling a bright window at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里飞蛾绕着一扇亮着的窗打转。

abstract.en: See a spotlight swing across a stage and stop on one singer.
abstract.cn: 想象一束追光扫过舞台，停在一个歌手身上。

examples.en: The bright stall attracted a crowd within minutes.
examples.cn: 明亮的摊位几分钟内就吸引了一群人。

examples.en: The flowers attract bees in early summer.
examples.cn: 初夏时这些花吸引蜜蜂。

examples.en: Bright colours attract young children.
examples.cn: 鲜艳的颜色会吸引小孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tract（拉）：把人和目光往自己这边拉，就是吸引；拉来的若是批评和麻烦，就是招致。

root: 源自拉丁语 attrahere，由 ad-「向」与 trahere「拉」构成，过去分词 attractus；经中古英语 attracten 进入英语，由「拉近」引申为引起兴趣，再引申为招致后果。

sensesIntro.en: A magnet, a headline and a careless remark all pull something toward them.
sensesIntro.cn: 磁石、标题和一句失言，都在把东西往自己这边拉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnet drawing iron filings into a tight ring.
core.cn: 核心意象：磁石把铁屑拉成一个紧贴的小圈。

intro.en: The root tract, 'to draw', links attract with distract and extract.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 意为「拉」，把 attract 与 distract、extract 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere, 'to draw', also gives tractor and traction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere「拉」也是 tractor 与 traction 的来源。

definition_zh: 吸引力；吸引人的事物（景点）；引力
definition_en: the power of something to interest or please people, a place or thing that draws visitors, or a force that pulls objects together
core_image: 游乐园里最高的那座塔，人群都朝它走过去
scene: 导游在车上指着窗外一片灯火，告诉大家下一个看点。The old castle is the town's main attraction.
sceneCN: 这里 attraction 是「吸引人的地方、景点」（第 2 个义项）；句意是这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。

senses.title: Pulling power
senses.definition: the quality that makes people feel interested or drawn to something
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生兴趣、被牵过去的那种性质
senses.example: The attraction of country life is its peace.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村生活的吸引力在于它的宁静。
senses.why: The noun names the force itself rather than the thing exerting it, so it can describe an abstract quality like peace or freedom.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指的是「力」本身，而不是发出这股力的东西，所以可以形容宁静、自由这类抽象特质。

senses.title: Place worth visiting
senses.definition: a place or thing that people visit because it is interesting
senses.definitionCN: 因为有趣而吸引人去参观的地方或事物
senses.example: The castle is the town's main attraction.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。
senses.why: The abstract pull is turned into a countable object: whatever does the pulling can be counted as one attraction among many.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的「拉力」被具体化成可数的东西：凡是发出吸引力的，都能算作众多景点中的一个。

senses.title: Force between objects
senses.definition: a force that makes objects move toward each other
senses.definitionCN: 使物体相互靠近的力
senses.example: Gravity is the force of attraction between masses.
senses.exampleCN: 重力是物体之间相互吸引的力。
senses.why: Physics kept the oldest and most literal part of the word: bodies really do pull one another, with no interest or feeling involved.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留了这个词最古老、最字面的部分：物体确实在互相拉，其中没有兴趣或情感。

intro.en: Attraction turns the act of drawing into a thing: the pull itself.
intro.cn: attraction 把「拉」这个动作变成一样东西：那股拉力本身。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw or pull'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、牵引」。

items.en: attrahere meant 'to draw toward'.
items.cn: attrahere 意为「拉向」。

items.en: attractio named the action of drawing something near.
items.cn: attractio 指「把东西拉近」这一动作。

items.en: French attraction carried the noun into English.
items.cn: 法语 attraction 把这个名词带进英语。

items.en: English added tourist sights and the force studied in physics.
items.cn: 英语又加上了旅游景点与物理学研究的作用力两层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tract root; the near-meaning group gives words for charm and appeal.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tract 词根；近义组是表示魅力与吸引的说法。

entries.definition: the act of drawing something out
a person or thing that attracts

normalIntro.en: Attraction is either the pull or the thing that pulls.
normalIntro.cn: attraction 要么指那股拉力，要么指发出拉力的东西。

normal.en: The ending -tion marks a noun built on the verb attract.
normal.cn: 词尾 -tion 表明这是由动词 attract 构成的名词。

normal.en: Tourist attraction is the phrase you will meet most often in travel texts.
normal.cn: 旅游文本里最常见的是 tourist attraction 这个搭配。

normal.en: Attraction to someone names a feeling of being drawn.
normal.cn: attraction to someone 表示被某人吸引的那种感觉。

normal.en: In physics, attraction is the opposite of repulsion.
normal.cn: 在物理学里，attraction 与 repulsion 相对。

normal.en: The verb is attract and the adjective is attractive.
normal.cn: 动词是 attract，形容词是 attractive。

abstract.en: See a lit fairground tower visible from every street.
abstract.cn: 想象一座亮着的游乐塔，从每条街都看得见。

abstract.en: See a crowd flowing like water toward one gate.
abstract.cn: 想象人群像水一样朝同一个门口流去。

abstract.en: See two magnets click together across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两块磁石隔着桌子啪地吸到一起。

examples.en: The attraction of country life is its peace.
examples.cn: 乡村生活的吸引力在于它的宁静。

examples.en: The castle is the town's main attraction.
examples.cn: 这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。

examples.en: Gravity is the force of attraction between masses.
examples.cn: 重力是物体之间相互吸引的力。

dict_mnemonic.text: attract 加 -ion 变成名词：那股把人拉过去的力量是吸引力，被拉过去看的地方就是景点。

root: 源自拉丁语 attractio，来自 attrahere「拉向」，词基 trahere 意为「拉」；经法语 attraction 进入英语，由「拉近的动作」引申为吸引力，再具体化为景点，并在物理学中指物体间的引力。

sensesIntro.en: One word covers the pull, the place that pulls, and the force between two bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既指拉力，也指发出拉力的地方，还指两个物体之间的作用力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd streaming toward one lit tower.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群朝一座亮着的塔涌过去。

intro.en: The root tract, 'to draw', runs through the whole attraction family.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 意为「拉」，贯穿 attraction 整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere also produced traction and tractor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 还产生了 traction 与 tractor。

items.meaning: the pull or the thing that pulls

definition_zh: 好看的；有魅力的；有吸引力的（条件、提议）
definition_en: pleasant to look at, or good enough to make people want it
core_image: 橱窗里的一件东西让人走过又退回来多看一眼
scene: 中介带人看房，一进门就被落地窗外的景色吸引。The flat is small but very attractive.
sceneCN: 这里 attractive 是「好看的、有魅力的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是这套公寓不大，但非常讨人喜欢。

pos.zh: 形容词：好看的；有吸引力的

senses.title: Pleasing to look at
senses.definition: pleasant in appearance, so that people enjoy looking at you or it
senses.definitionCN: 外表讨人喜欢，让人愿意多看
senses.example: She wore a simple but attractive dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一条简单却很好看的连衣裙。
senses.why: The word describes the effect on the viewer: something attractive draws the eye before any judgment is made about it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是看的人受到的影响：有魅力的东西先抓住目光，人才会去评判它。

senses.title: Worth accepting
senses.definition: good enough to make people want to accept it or join in
senses.definitionCN: 条件足够好，让人愿意接受或参与
senses.example: They made us an attractive offer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给了我们一个很有吸引力的报价。
senses.why: The pull is no longer visual but practical: a price, a job or a deal can attract a person just as a face can.
senses.whyCN: 这里的吸引力不再是视觉上的，而是实际利益上的：价格、工作或交易也像面容一样能把人拉过来。

intro.en: Attractive simply means having the power to draw.
intro.cn: attractive 的意思就是「具有拉过来的力量」。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw or pull'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、牵引」。

items.en: attractus was the participle 'drawn toward'.
items.cn: attractus 是表示「被拉近」的分词。

items.en: attractivus described something with power to draw.
items.cn: attractivus 描述「具有吸引力」的东西。

items.en: French attractif carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 attractif 把这个形容词带进英语。

items.en: English widened it from physical pull to beauty and good deals.
items.cn: 英语把它从物理拉力扩展到美貌与划算的条件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that sound close; the near-meaning group holds words of beauty and appeal.
note.cn: 形近组是读音相近的词；近义组是表示美貌与吸引力的词。

normalIntro.en: Anything that draws people can be called attractive, from a face to a salary.
normalIntro.cn: 凡是能把人吸引过来的，从面容到薪水，都可以叫 attractive。

normal.en: The ending -ive makes it an adjective describing what does the attracting.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 使它成为形容词，描述发出吸引力的那一方。

normal.en: Use attractive to before the person or group being drawn.
normal.cn: 用 attractive to 引出被吸引的人或群体。

normal.en: An attractive offer is about terms, not looks.
normal.cn: attractive offer 说的是条件，不是长相。

normal.en: The noun is attraction and the verb is attract.
normal.cn: 名词是 attraction，动词是 attract。

normal.en: Do not mix it up with attentive, which means watching closely.
normal.cn: 不要与 attentive 混淆，后者意为专心留意。

abstract.en: See a shop window that stops people in the middle of a step.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇橱窗让人走到一半就停下来。

abstract.en: See a price tag that makes a buyer smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一个价签让买家笑起来。

abstract.en: See a face turn a whole room without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸一句话不说就让整个房间转过头来。

examples.en: The flat is small but very attractive.
examples.cn: 这套公寓不大，但非常讨人喜欢。

examples.en: She wore a simple but attractive dress.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条简单却很好看的连衣裙。

examples.en: They made us an attractive offer.
examples.cn: 他们给了我们一个很有吸引力的报价。

dict_mnemonic.text: attract 加 -ive：会把人拉过来的，就是有吸引力的；拉眼睛的是好看，拉钱包的是条件划算。

root: 源自拉丁语 attractivus「有吸引力的」，来自 attrahere「拉向」，词基 trahere 意为「拉」；经法语 attractif 进入英语，由物理拉力扩展到外貌与条件的吸引力。

sensesIntro.en: A beautiful face and a generous salary pull people in the same grammatical way.
sensesIntro.cn: 一张好看的脸和一份优厚的薪水，在语法上是以同一种方式把人拉过去的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop window that makes a walker turn back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇橱窗让路人回头。

intro.en: The root tract, 'to draw', is the same one heard in attract and distraction.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 意为「拉」，在 attract 与 distraction 里听到的是同一个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere also gives tractor, traction and extract.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 还给出 tractor、traction 与 extract。

definition_zh: adj. 可归因于……的；可归属于某人或某单位的
definition_en: Able to be regarded as caused by, or as belonging to, a stated person or factor.
core_image: 一条箭头把结果指回它的来处
scene: 报告说这轮减产大半可归因于早霜。The report said the shortfall was largely attributable to the early frost.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attributable 指某结果能够被认定由某个原因造成，常与 to 连用。

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Traceable to a cause
senses.definition: of a result or effect that can reasonably be said to be caused by a stated factor
senses.definitionCN: 指结果或影响可以合理地被认定由某个因素造成
senses.example: Half the delay was attributable to bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 一半的延误可归因于恶劣天气。
senses.why: Attribute means to assign to, so adding -able gives the sense of a result that can be assigned back to a cause.
senses.whyCN: attribute 意为「归于」，加上 -able 便指某个结果能够被归回一个原因。

senses.title: Assignable to an owner
senses.definition: of income, costs or work that can be credited or charged to a particular person or unit
senses.definitionCN: 指收入、成本或工作可以记入某个人员或单位名下
senses.example: Only costs attributable to the project were repaid.
senses.exampleCN: 只有可归属该项目的成本获得报销。
senses.why: Accounting kept the assigning sense but dropped the causal one, so the arrow points to an owner instead of a cause.
senses.whyCN: 会计沿用「归属」义而舍去因果义，于是箭头指向所有者而非原因。

intro.en: Attributable is attribute plus -able; attribute comes from Latin attribuere, to assign to, from ad-, to, and tribuere, to allot, from tribus, tribe.
intro.cn: attributable 是 attribute 加 -able；attribute 来自拉丁语 attribuere「归于」，由 ad-「向」与 tribuere「分派」构成，而 tribuere 出自 tribus「部族」。

items.en: Latin tribus meant a tribe, one of the divisions among which goods and duties were shared out.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tribus 意为「部族」，即分配财物与义务时所依据的划分之一。

items.en: From it came tribuere, to assign or grant, originally to allot among the tribes.
items.cn: 由此产生 tribuere「分配、授予」，本义是按部族分派。

items.en: With ad-, to, added, attribuere meant to assign to, to attach a thing to its source.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」构成 attribuere「归于」，即把事物挂到它的来源上。

items.en: The participle attributus, assigned, is the form English took as its base.
items.cn: 分词 attributus「已被归于的」是英语取用的基础形式。

items.en: English adopted attribute in the fifteenth century as a verb and, later, as a noun.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪采用 attribute 作动词，后来又作名词。

items.en: The adjective with -able appears in the seventeenth century, chiefly in reasoning about causes.
items.cn: 带 -able 的形容词出现在十七世纪，主要用于因果推断。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the tribute family; the near-meaning group lists other words for something that can be traced back to a source.
note.cn: 形近组保留 tribute 词族；近义组列出其他表示可追溯到某来源的词。

entries.definition: The act of assigning a cause.
Used as a modifier before a noun.
To give a share towards a result.
Able to be credited to a source.
Able to be charged to someone.
Required to answer for a result.

normalIntro.en: Attributable is attribute plus -able: if a result can be attributed to something, it is attributable to it.
normalIntro.cn: attributable 是 attribute 加 -able：结果能被归到某原因，它就是可归因于该原因的。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is attributable to plus a cause.
normal.cn: 固定句式是 attributable to 加原因。

normal.en: Directly and largely are the commonest adverbs.
normal.cn: directly 与 largely 是最常见的搭配副词。

normal.en: Attributable risk is a set epidemiology term.
normal.cn: attributable risk 是流行病学术语。

normal.en: The noun is attribution, not attributableness.
normal.cn: 名词是 attribution，不用 attributableness。

normal.en: The negative form is unattributable.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unattributable。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn from effect back to cause.
abstract.cn: 想象一支从结果指回原因的箭头。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger line charged to one project.
abstract.cn: 想象账簿上一笔记入某项目的支出。

abstract.en: Think of a label tied to a single source.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚系在唯一来源上的标签。

examples.en: The gain is attributable to lower costs.
examples.cn: 这项收益可归因于成本下降。

examples.en: Deaths attributable to heat rose sharply.
examples.cn: 可归因于高温的死亡人数急升。

examples.en: Revenue attributable to the region was small.
examples.cn: 可归属该地区的收入很少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：at-「向」+ tribute「分派」+ -able「可……的」——能把结果分派回某原因的，就是 attributable。

root: 拉丁语 tribus「部族」生出 tribuere「按部族分派」，加 ad-「向」成 attribuere「归于」；英语 attribute 再加 -able，表示结果可被归回某原因或某主体。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses draw the same arrow backwards: from an effect to its cause, and from money or work to its owner.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项画的是同一支向后的箭头：从结果指向原因，从款项或工作指向其归属者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow pointing a result back to where it came from
core.cn: 核心意象：一条箭头把结果指回它的来处

branches.en: A shortfall traced to early frost.
Both send the result back to a source.
branches.cn: 两者都把结果送回某个来源。

intro.en: Attributable is at- plus tribute plus -able; the tribute root also builds contribute, distribute and retribution.
intro.cn: attributable 是 at- 加 tribute 加 -able；tribute 词根还构成 contribute、distribute 与 retribution。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tribus, tribe, tribuere, to allot, and attribuere, to assign to; -able is the Latin -abilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tribus「部族」、tribuere「分派」与 attribuere「归于」；-able 即拉丁语 -abilis。

definition_zh: 属性，特质；把……归因于；认为（作品）出自……
definition_en: a quality that belongs to a person or thing, or to say that something is caused by or made by someone
core_image: 一件物品上系着标签，写着它是什么、从哪里来
scene: 老师在评语里写下这个学生最突出的特点。Patience is the attribute every good teacher needs.
sceneCN: 这里 attribute 是「特质、属性」（第 1 个义项）；句意是耐心是每位好老师都需要的特质。

pos.zh: 动词：把……归因于；认为出自

senses.title: Mark of a thing
senses.definition: a quality or feature that belongs to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人或某物的性质或特征
senses.example: Kindness was his most striking attribute.
senses.exampleCN: 善良是他最突出的特质。
senses.why: The noun keeps the old sense of something allotted to a thing: an attribute is a quality assigned to whatever carries it.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「分派给某物」的旧义：属性就是分配给承载者的那种性质。

senses.title: Name the cause
senses.definition: to say that something is the result of a particular cause
senses.definitionCN: 认为某结果是某个原因造成的
senses.example: She attributes her success to hard work.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己的成功归功于努力。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction: instead of giving a quality to a thing, you give an effect back to the cause that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把方向倒过来：不是把性质给某物，而是把一个结果送回造成它的原因。

senses.title: Name the maker
senses.definition: to believe that a work was produced by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认为某件作品是由某个特定的人创作的
senses.example: The painting was attributed to an unknown artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画被认定出自一位不知名的画家之手。
senses.why: Authorship is treated as another kind of allotment: the work is assigned back to the hand that made it.
senses.whyCN: 作者身份被视为另一种「分派」：把作品重新分配给做出它的那只手。

intro.en: Attribute began as a legal word for something allotted to a person.
intro.cn: attribute 最初是个法律用语，指分派给某人的东西。

items.en: tribuere meant 'to allot or assign'.
items.cn: tribuere 意为「分配、分派」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus tribuere made attribuere, 'to assign to'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 tribuere 构成 attribuere，意为「分派给」。

items.en: attributum was the thing assigned or credited.
items.cn: attributum 指被分派或归到某人名下的东西。

items.en: French attribut named a quality belonging to something.
items.cn: 法语 attribut 指属于某物的性质。

items.en: English split the word into a noun of quality and a verb of assigning causes.
items.cn: 英语把它分成表示性质的名词与表示归因的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tribute root; the near-meaning group gives nouns of quality and verbs of explaining causes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tribute 词根；近义组是表示性质的名词与解释原因的动词。

normalIntro.cn: 作名词时它指一种性质；作动词时它把结果交还给原因。

normal.en: The noun stresses the first syllable, the verb the second.
normal.cn: 作名词时重音在第一音节，作动词时重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Attribute to is the verb pattern: attribute success to luck.
normal.cn: 动词搭配是 attribute to，例如把成功归因于运气。

normal.en: An attribute is something a person or thing simply has.

normal.en: To attribute a painting to an artist is to name its maker.
normal.cn: 把画作归到某位画家名下，就是认定它的作者。

normal.en: The root tribute means to give or allot.
normal.cn: 词根 tribute 意为「给予、分配」。

abstract.en: See a label tied to an object, naming what it is.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签系在物品上，写明它是什么。

abstract.en: See a line drawn from an effect back to its cause.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线从结果往回连到原因。

abstract.en: See a signature appear under a painting that had none.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅原本无款的画作下方浮现出签名。

sensesIntro.en: The same act of allotting produces both a quality and an explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「分配」的动作，既产生了一种性质，也产生了一种解释。

definition_zh: 大胆的；放肆的；敢于冒险的；出格的
definition_en: showing a willingness to take bold or surprising risks; showing too much confidence or disrespect
core_image: 明知不该却偏要迈出那一步的人：既有胆量，也有点冒犯
scene: 颁奖礼上，无名新人竟当众指出评委的方案漏洞。An audacious young architect questioned the judges' design in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 audacious 指「大胆敢言、近乎放肆的」（第 1 个义项：敢作敢当的胆量）；句意：一个胆大包天的年轻建筑师当众质疑评委的设计。

pos.zh: 大胆的；敢于冒险的；放肆的

derivatives.zh: 大胆；放肆（audacious + -ity 名词后缀）
大胆地；放肆地（audacious + -ly 副词后缀）
大胆；放肆（audacious + -ness 名词后缀）
拉丁语原词「大胆的」（仅用于学名与引文）

senses.title: Bold and willing to take risks
senses.definition: showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks
senses.definitionCN: 表现出敢于承担惊人风险的胆量的
senses.example: It was audacious of them to launch the company with no money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们身无分文就敢开公司，真是胆大。
senses.why: The Latin root audax means bold; the core image is the courage to step where others hesitate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 audax 意为「大胆」；核心意象是敢在别人犹豫之处迈步的胆量。

senses.title: Showing disrespect or lack of shame
senses.definition: showing too much confidence or a lack of respect, often in a shocking way
senses.definitionCN: 表现出过分的自信或不敬，常令人震惊的
senses.example: She had the audacious nerve to ask for a raise on her first day.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一天上班就敢开口要加薪，实在放肆。
senses.why: The same boldness can offend when it crosses social lines; the word keeps both faces.
senses.whyCN: 同样的胆量一旦越过社会界线便会冒犯人；这个词始终保有两张面孔。

senses.title: Original and striking in style
senses.definition: of art, fashion, or ideas, strikingly original and unconventional
senses.definitionCN: （艺术、时尚、思想）极其新颖、不循常规的
senses.example: The director made an audacious film with no dialogue at all.
senses.exampleCN: 导演拍了一部全程无对白的大胆电影。
senses.why: In creative fields, breaking rules is the visible form of daring, so the word drifted to style.
senses.whyCN: 在创作领域，打破常规是胆识最直观的形态，词义于是滑向风格。

senses.title: Of actions of breathtaking daring
senses.definition: of a crime, plan, or exploit, so bold that it amazes people
senses.definitionCN: （罪行、计划、壮举）大胆到令人咋舌的
senses.example: The museum theft was an audacious daytime raid.
senses.exampleCN: 那起博物馆失窃案是一次光天化日下的胆大行窃。
senses.why: When daring is aimed at forbidden goals, admiration and shock mix in one word.
senses.whyCN: 当胆量瞄准禁忌目标时，惊叹与震骇便在同一词中交织。

senses.title: Cheeky or impudent in speech
senses.titleCN: 嘴上冒犯的；没大没小的
senses.definition: of a remark or question, rude in a bold, often amusing way
senses.definitionCN: （言辞、提问）大胆而近乎无礼、常带滑稽感的
senses.example: The child asked the audacious question everyone else avoided.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子问出了所有大人都在回避的大胆问题。
senses.why: Children and comedians borrow this boldness harmlessly, giving the word a lighter shade.
senses.whyCN: 孩子和喜剧演员把这份胆量用得毫无恶意，词义因此添了一层轻松色彩。

senses.title: Defying the odds
senses.titleCN: 逆势而为的；明知不可为而为之的
senses.definition: undertaken despite overwhelming difficulty or opposition
senses.definitionCN: 不顾压倒性的困难或反对而进行的
senses.example: Their audacious escape from the besieged city became legend.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从被围之城大胆出逃，成了传奇。
senses.why: Real daring shows itself only against odds, so the word attaches to improbable ventures.
senses.whyCN: 真正的胆识只有在悬殊的劣势前才显形，词义便落在那些看似不可能的行动上。

senses.title: Confident to the point of arrogance
senses.definition: marked by confidence so high it seems like arrogance
senses.definitionCN: 自信过头、近乎傲慢的
senses.example: He closed his speech with an audacious promise to end poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一句终结贫困的大话结束了演讲。
senses.why: When the bold voice exceeds its evidence, listeners hear arrogance rather than courage.
senses.whyCN: 当大胆的宣言超出证据所能支撑时，听者听到的就是傲慢而非勇气。

senses.title: Admirably inventive
senses.definition: of a solution or stroke, daring in a way that earns admiration
senses.definitionCN: （解法、妙手）因敢于打破常规而赢得赞叹的
senses.example: The audacious final move won the chess match.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那步大胆的走法赢下了棋局。
senses.why: The bright side of audax is creative risk-taking; chess and strategy keep it alive.
senses.whyCN: audax 光明的一面是创造性的冒险；棋局与谋略让这层意思留存至今。

intro.en: Audacious comes from the Latin adjective audax, bold, built on audere, to dare; English borrowed it through the related noun audacia in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: audacious 源自拉丁语形容词 audax「大胆的」，其核心是动词 audere「敢」；16 世纪英语经由相关名词 audacia 借入该词。

items.en: The root *awej- meant to be eager or to dare, pointing toward bold desire and confidence.
items.cn: 词根 *awej- 意为「渴望、敢于」，指向大胆的欲望与自信。

items.en: audere meant to dare, and its adjective audax (genitive audacis) meant bold or daring.
items.cn: 拉丁语 audere 意为「敢」，其形容词 audax（属格 audacis）意为「大胆的、敢作敢为的」。

items.en: The noun audacia meant boldness, both the noble courage and the shameless forwardness.
items.cn: 名词 audacia 意为「大胆」，兼指高尚的勇气与无耻的放肆。

items.en: English took audacious and audacity together in the mid-sixteenth century, keeping the double sense of courage and impudence.
items.cn: 16 世纪中叶英语同时借入 audacious 与 audacity，勇气与无礼的双重意味一并保留。

items.en: Writers used it of bold soldiers and of presumptuous claims alike, fixing the word's two faces.
items.cn: 作家既用它写勇猛的将士，也用它写狂妄的断言，双面含义就此固定。

items.en: Modern usage praises audacious artists and entrepreneurs while still using it to scold the rude.
items.cn: 现代用法既赞艺术家的胆识、创业者的果敢，也仍用它斥责无礼之人。

note.en: Group one collects look-alikes from the dare family and words sharing the aud- spelling by accident; group two collects neighboring bold words.
note.cn: 第一组收「敢」字族及拼写恰好同以 aud- 开头的词；第二组收相邻的大胆类词。

entries.definition: the noun form: boldness or shameless daring.
entries.definitionCN: audacious 的名词形式：大胆；放肆。

entries.definition: able to be heard, from Latin audire, to hear; only the aud- spelling is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 听得见的，出自拉丁语 audire「听」；只是拼写同以 aud- 开头，词源不同。

entries.definition: relating to sound; from the hear root, not the dare root.
entries.definitionCN: 音频的；出自「听」的词根，与「敢」的词根无关。

entries.definition: majestic and venerable, from Latin augere, to increase; not from audax.
entries.definitionCN: 威严的；令人敬畏的，出自拉丁语 augere「增长」，与 audax 无关。

entries.definition: fearless and adventurous; the plain everyday term.
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢的；大胆的；最常用的日常说法。
勇于冒险的；多含赞赏之意。

entries.definition: bold without shame; heavier on the impudence side.
entries.definitionCN: 厚颜无耻的；更侧重无礼一面。

entries.definition: fearless, especially of explorers and heroes.
entries.definitionCN: 无畏的；多用于探险家与英雄。

entries.definition: bold without thought of danger or consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 鲁莽的；不计后果的大胆，多含贬义。

normalIntro.en: audacious keeps its Latin heart audax, bold, visible in audacity and the aud- spelling.
normalIntro.cn: audacious 保留拉丁语心脏 audax「大胆」，在 audacity 与 aud- 拼写中清晰可见。

normal.en: audax to audacious: dare first, then add the adjective ending.
normal.cn: 从 audax 到 audacious：先「敢」，再加形容词词尾。

normal.en: The -acious ending recurs in tenacious and vivacious, all meaning full of something.
normal.cn: -acious 词尾常见于 tenacious、vivacious，都表示「充满某性质」。

normal.en: audacity is the noun you reach for when someone dares too much.
normal.cn: 当某人胆子太大时，你会脱口而出它的名词 audacity。

normal.en: An audacious plan is bold enough to make people gasp.
normal.cn: 大胆的计划胆量大到让人倒吸一口气。

normal.en: Its twin senses: courage you admire, nerve you scold.
normal.cn: 双生含义：一面是你赞赏的勇气，一面是你训斥的放肆。

abstract.en: Picture someone stepping off a cliff-edge ledge others refuse to touch.
abstract.cn: 想象有人踩上众人不敢碰的悬崖边缘。

abstract.en: The word itself leans forward, like a hand raised before permission is given.
abstract.cn: 这个词本身向前倾，像未经允许就先举起的手。

abstract.en: Audacious is a tightrope between hero and nuisance.
abstract.cn: audacious 是英雄与讨厌鬼之间的一根钢丝。

examples.en: It was audacious of the junior clerk to rewrite the director's report.
examples.cn: 那个小职员胆子真大，竟敢重写主管的报告。

examples.en: The audacious jailbreak was planned in a single night.
examples.cn: 这场胆大包天的越狱仅一夜之间便策划完成。

examples.en: Critics praised the band's audacious blend of opera and punk.
examples.cn: 评论家盛赞该乐队将歌剧与朋克大胆融合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「傲地死」——傲慢到地上打滚也要坚持大胆发言，胆大放肆到极点

root: 出自拉丁语 audax「大胆的」（属格 audacis），核心为动词 audere「敢」；经其派生名词 audacia「大胆；放肆」于 16 世纪进入英语，与 audacity 同族，属「敢」词根一系，词源确凿。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all grow from one root meaning bold: from admired courage through impudent nerve to inventive brilliance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「大胆」这一词根生长：从受人赞叹的勇气，到近乎无礼的放肆，再到令人叫绝的独创。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping forward when everyone else steps back.
core.cn: 核心意象：众人后退时，偏要向前迈出一步。

branches.en: THE COURAGE SIDE: bold ventures and improbable escapes.
branches.cn: 勇气一面：大胆的事业与看似不可能的出逃。

branches.en: THE NERVE SIDE: remarks and demands that cross the line.
branches.cn: 放肆一面：越界的言辞与要求。

branches.en: THE CREATIVE SIDE: art and moves that break rules and win praise.
branches.cn: 创造一面：打破常规、赢得赞叹的艺术与妙手。

branches.en: THE CRIME SIDE: exploits so bold they amaze.
branches.cn: 惊世一面：大胆到令人咋舌的行径。

branches.en: THE ARROGANCE SIDE: confidence that outruns its proof.
branches.cn: 傲慢一面：超出证据的自信。

intro.en: audacious is audax plus -acious, an adjective ending meaning full of; the dare root is the whole engine of the word.
intro.cn: audacious 由 audax 加 -acious 构成，后者是表示「充满某性质」的形容词词尾；「敢」的词根是全词的发动机。

latinIntro.en: Latin audere, to dare, is the anchor: audax, audacia, and English audacious and audacity all descend from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audere「敢」是家族之锚：audax、audacia，以及英语的 audacious、audacity 皆出于此。

definition_zh: 听得见的；可闻的
definition_en: able to be heard; loud or clear enough to reach the ear
core_image: 声音越过距离传到耳朵里：能被听见
scene: 后排的家长踮起脚，仍听不清台上的致辞。The speaker's voice was barely audible over the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 audible 指「听得见的」（第 1 个义项：声音可被听到）；句意：演讲者的声音在风里几乎听不见。

derivatives.zh: 听不见的（in- 否定前缀 + audible）
听众；观众（同族词，出自 audire「听」）

senses.title: Loud enough to hear
senses.definition: loud or clear enough to be heard
senses.definitionCN: 响亮或清晰到足以被听见的
senses.example: Her voice was barely audible at the back of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 在礼堂后排几乎听不见她的声音。
senses.why: The root audire means to hear; -able marks what can undergo it.
senses.whyCN: 词根 audire 意为「听」；-able 标记「可被……的」。

senses.title: Within human hearing range
senses.definition: of sound waves, within the range humans can perceive
senses.definitionCN: （声波）处于人耳可感知范围内的
senses.example: Dogs hear frequencies well beyond the audible range.
senses.exampleCN: 狗能听到远超人耳听域的频率。
senses.why: Physics fixed the word to a measured band: too high or too low is inaudible.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个词锚定在一段可测的频带：过高过低都不可闻。

senses.title: Expressed out loud
senses.definition: of a feeling, made audible as a sound, such as a sigh or groan
senses.definitionCN: （情绪）以叹息、呻吟等声音形式发出来的
senses.example: She gave an audible sigh of relief.
senses.exampleCN: 她如释重负，发出一声听得见的叹息。
senses.why: Silent feelings become audible the moment they escape as sound.
senses.whyCN: 无声的情绪一旦化作声音逸出，便成为「可闻」的。

senses.title: Clearly heard by listeners
senses.definition: of speech or broadcast sound, clear enough for an audience
senses.definitionCN: （讲话、广播声音）对听众足够清晰的
senses.example: Check that every speaker is audible from the last row.
senses.exampleCN: 确认每位发言人的声音在最后一排都能听清。
senses.why: In public speaking the test is the farthest ear, so the word measures reach.
senses.whyCN: 公开演讲的检验标准是最远的那只耳朵，这个词便成了「传到与否」的量尺。

senses.title: Perceptible in recordings
senses.definition: of a sound in a recording, present and distinguishable on playback
senses.definitionCN: （录音中的声音）回放时存在且可分辨的
senses.example: A second voice is faintly audible in the background of the tape.
senses.exampleCN: 磁带背景里隐约能听到第二个声音。
senses.why: Recordings create a second ear, and audible now marks what survives onto it.
senses.whyCN: 录音创造了第二只耳朵，audible 如今标记能在这只耳朵上留痕的声音。

senses.title: Detectable by instruments of hearing
senses.definition: of a signal, present in the audio channel or detectable as sound
senses.definitionCN: （信号）存在于音频通道或可作为声音检出的
senses.example: An audible warning sounds when the door is not closed.
senses.exampleCN: 车门未关好时会响起声音警报。
senses.why: Engineering needs an adjective for signals the ear can catch, and this one fits.
senses.whyCN: 工程上需要一个形容词来指耳朵能捕捉的信号，这个词正合适。

senses.title: Easily heard, emphasized
senses.definition: used with negatives or adverbs to grade how well a sound carries
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词或副词连用，为声音的传达程度分等
senses.example: His whisper was just audible over the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨声中他的低语勉强可闻。
senses.why: Hearing is a gradient, so the word lives with barely, faintly, and just.
senses.whyCN: 听觉本是个渐变量，这个词便常与 barely、faintly、just 为伴。

senses.title: In sports, a called play
senses.titleCN: （美式橄榄球）临场喊出的战术
senses.definition: in American football, an audible is a play called at the line of scrimmage
senses.definitionCN: 美式橄榄球中指在开阵线前临场改喊的战术
senses.example: The quarterback called an audible seconds before the snap.
senses.exampleCN: 开球前几秒，四分卫临场改喊了战术。
senses.why: A play that exists only as a shouted word is literally made of hearing.
senses.whyCN: 只存在于一声喊叫里的战术，名副其实地由「听」构成。

intro.en: Audible comes from Latin audibilis, formed on audire, to hear; English borrowed it from the Latin past participle stem audit- plus -ibilis in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: audible 出自拉丁语 audibilis，其基础是动词 audire「听」；15 世纪英语从拉丁语过去分词词干 audit- 加 -ibilis 将其借入。

items.en: The root *h₂ewis- meant to perceive, to hear, feeding the Latin hearing family.
items.cn: 词根 *h₂ewis- 意为「感知、听见」，孕育了拉丁语「听」的词族。

items.en: audire meant to hear; its participle stem audit- and adjective audibilis meant able to be heard.
items.cn: 拉丁语 audire 意为「听」；其分词词干 audit- 与形容词 audibilis 意为「可被听见的」。

items.en: audibilis joined the verb stem with -ibilis, the standard Latin ending for able to be.
items.cn: audibilis 由动词词干加 -ibilis 构成，后者是拉丁语表示「可……的」的标准词尾。

items.en: audible entered English in the fifteenth century, first in learned and religious texts.
items.cn: audible 于 15 世纪进入英语，最初见于学术与宗教文本。

items.en: Science and music widened its use to measured ranges of sound.
items.cn: 科学与音乐把它扩展到可测量的声音范围。

items.en: From radio engineering to football play-calling, audible now marks every sound that reaches an ear or channel.
items.cn: 从无线电工程到橄榄球战术口令，audible 如今标记一切能抵达耳朵或声道的信号。

note.en: Group one collects the hear-family and the aud- look-alikes from the dare root; group two collects neighboring hearing words.
note.cn: 第一组收「听」词族及与「敢」词根同以 aud- 开头的形近词；第二组收相邻的听觉词。

entries.definition: a group of listeners, from Latin audientia, a hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 听众；观众，出自拉丁语 audientia「听」。

entries.definition: the hall where people listen, literally the hearing place.
entries.definitionCN: 礼堂；听众席，本义即「听的地方」。

entries.definition: bold, from Latin audax, to dare; shares only the aud- spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的，出自拉丁语 audax「敢」；仅拼写同以 aud- 开头。

entries.definition: relating to the sense of hearing.
clearly heard or seen, easily told apart.
able to be noticed by any sense, hearing included.
deep, full, and resonant in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 浑厚响亮的；低沉有回响的。

entries.definition: too faint or high or low to be heard.
entries.definitionCN: 听不见的；audible 的反义词。

entries.definition: of the ear and hearing as a sense, not of a single sound.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉层面的；与单一声音相对。

normalIntro.en: audible wears its root on its sleeve: audi means hear, able means can.
normalIntro.cn: audible 把词根写在脸上：audi「听」+ able「能够」。

normal.en: audi + able: able to be heard, exactly as visible means able to be seen.
normal.cn: audi + able：能被听见，正如 visible 是能被看见。

normal.en: The audi family: audience, auditorium, audio, audible, all about hearing.
normal.cn: audi 家族：audience、auditorium、audio、audible——都关于「听」。

normal.en: Add in- and the sound vanishes: inaudible.
normal.cn: 加上 in- 声音便消失：inaudible。

normal.en: barely audible is the everyday phrase for a voice that hardly carries.
normal.cn: barely audible 是形容声音几乎传不到的日常说法。

normal.en: In football an audible is a play you can only know by hearing it.
normal.cn: 橄榄球里的 audible 是只能靠听来领会的战术。

abstract.en: Picture a sound crossing a noisy square and still arriving at one ear.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音穿过嘈杂广场，仍抵达了一只耳朵。

abstract.en: Audible is the moment silence breaks.
abstract.cn: audible 是寂静被打破的那一刻。

abstract.en: Think of a volume knob: audible is anywhere above zero.
abstract.cn: 把它想成音量旋钮：零以上皆为 audible。

examples.en: The teacher's voice stayed audible even at the back of the playground.
examples.cn: 即使在操场尽头，老师的声音也清晰可闻。

examples.en: There was an audible gasp when the results appeared on the screen.
examples.cn: 结果出现在屏幕上时，全场响起清晰的倒吸气声。

examples.en: The recording was old, but every word remained audible.
examples.cn: 录音年代久远，但每个字仍然听得清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥弟」——奥秘弟在外屋大声唱歌，隔着门也听得见

root: 出自拉丁语 audire「听」（过去分词词干 audit-）+ 形容词后缀 -ibilis「可……的」，即 audibilis「可被听见的」；15 世纪进入英语，与 audience、audio、auditorium 同属「听」词族，词源确凿。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hearing adjective: from sheer loudness through measured ranges and escaped sighs to the football call that lives only in sound.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟随一个「听」的形容词：从纯粹的响度，到可测的频带、逸出的叹息，再到只存在于声音里的橄榄球战术口令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound that completes its journey to an ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：完成抵达耳朵之旅的声音。

branches.en: THE LOUDNESS SCALE: barely audible to clearly audible.
branches.cn: 响度标尺：从勉强可闻到清晰可闻。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SIDE: hearing ranges, warnings, and signals.
branches.cn: 可测一面：听域、警报与信号。

branches.en: ESCAPED SOUND: sighs and background voices on tape.
branches.cn: 逸出的声音：叹息与磁带里的背景人声。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCE SIDE: speech that must reach the last row.
branches.cn: 听众一面：必须传到最后一排的讲话。

branches.en: THE FIELD SIDE: the football play called in a shout.
branches.cn: 赛场一面：一声喊出的橄榄球战术。

intro.en: audible is built transparently: the verb stem audi- plus -able, exactly parallel to visible and readable.
intro.cn: audible 结构一目了然：动词词干 audi- 加 -able，与 visible、readable 完全平行。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, to hear, anchors a wide family: audience, audio, auditory, auditorium, audition, and audible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire「听」统率一个庞大词族：audience、audio、auditory、auditorium、audition 与 audible。
